entry.summary: Electronic-Structure-Informed Many-Body Encoding for Quantum Machine Learning arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces a physics-informed quantum encoding that uses the many-body structure of electronic systems, linking the body order of input descriptors to the locality of quantum gates. Descriptors from a single mean-field calculation are encoded with one- to four-body circuits and used to predict electron-correlation energies along bond-stretching potential energy surfaces. The authors report that higher-order encodings systematically improve accuracy toward the full configuration interaction limit.

entry.title: Using the Wigner function to certify and measure stellar rank
entry.summary: Witnessing and quantifying stellar rank with the Wigner function arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents a method to witness and quantify non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum systems using displaced parity measurements, applied to superconducting cavity data. It also introduces refined witnesses that measure the Wigner function at a few points. The techniques are applied to Fock, binomial, cat, and GKP states, establishing a stellar rank of 8 for a GKP state.

entry.title: Beyond the Kubo formula: unifying adiabatic and isothermal quantum responses
entry.summary: Beyond the Kubo formula: unification of adiabatic and isothermal response in quantum systems arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper notes that the static limit of the Kubo susceptibility describes the adiabatic response of an isolated quantum system, which generally differs from the isothermal response where energy-level occupations readjust to thermal equilibrium. The authors introduce a single dynamical framework, an open-system version of the Kubo approach in which dissipation is governed by the system's thermalization rate, so that adiabatic and isothermal responses appear as two distinct limiting regimes. They apply the method to the magnetic response of the electron gas and reproduce the expected results.

entry.title: Liouvillian spectral snapshots: a reduced-subspace method for time-dependent, noisy quantum systems
entry.summary: Liouvillian spectral snapshots: A reduced-subspace approach for time-dependent and noisy open quantum systems arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces Liouvillian spectral snapshots (LSS), a reduced-basis method for simulating driven-dissipative quantum systems under time-dependent drives and temporally correlated classical noise. LSS computes slowly decaying, low-frequency eigenoperators of the Liouvillian at a few adaptively sampled perturbation values and compresses them into a common basis. This projects the master equation onto a low-dimensional subspace, and the basis can be reused across noise realizations and parameters, lowering the cost of ensemble averages and parameter sweeps.

entry.title: How widely quantum states spread across possible configurations in Rydberg-atom systems, and how an added field changes this
entry.summary: Fock-space delocalization and its control in scarred-vs-ergodic dynamics arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The study examines PXP dynamics in Rydberg-atom arrays, measuring the fraction of allowed configurations occupied between revivals. Starting from the polarized state, dynamics fill a finite fraction limited to one third by chiral symmetry, which rises to one half with a weak quasiperiodic field. Starting from the Néel state, dynamics occupy a vanishing fraction in the thermodynamic limit and need a stronger field to reach a comparable regime. Beyond a certain field strength, the occupied fraction decreases for both initial states.

entry.title: Unifying methods for quantum systems interacting with quantum clocks
entry.summary: Relating approaches to interacting quantum clocks and systems arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines how to describe the dynamics of a quantum system relative to a quantum clock it interacts with, a problem relevant to quantum reference frames and quantum gravity. It shows that approaches by Smith and Ahmadi, by Gemsheim and Rost, and the Born-Oppenheimer approach can be unified in one framework for conditional quantum states. The Born-Oppenheimer approach to quantum cosmology is identified with a type of interacting Page-Wootters formalism. The paper also discusses unitarity and linearity in relational dynamics.

entry.title: Spin state switch in rotating moiré atoms under a magnetic field
entry.summary: Singlet-Triplet Transition of Rotating Moiré Atoms in a Magnetic Field arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Moiré superlattices can trap several electrons in each potential well, forming few-electron "moiré atoms." Using neural quantum states, the authors map the ground state of two-electron moiré atoms as a function of well depth and magnetic field strength. At strong field, the atoms are spin-triplet with a persistent circulating current, while deeper wells drive a transition to non-rotating spin-singlet atoms. At the transition, the orbital magnetic moments reverse sign, a signature that magnetometry could detect.

entry.title: Gapless and non-equilibrium topology in blockaded ladder systems
entry.summary: Gapless and Non-Equilibrium Topology in Blockaded Ladders arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes a multi-leg PXYP model as a minimal setting for studying how constraints link mobile particles and internal degrees of freedom. The authors argue that Rydberg-like blockade induces correlations in squeezed space, providing a unified mechanism for string order in and out of equilibrium. In a two-leg geometry this yields an intrinsically gapless topological ground state that can end at a supersymmetric multicritical point, while a three-leg geometry gives an emergent U(1) symmetry and a multicomponent Luttinger liquid.

entry.title: Quantum version of converse symmetry breaking: adding coupling mismatches to boost quantum synchronization
entry.summary: Quantum manifestations of converse symmetry breaking arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies quantum synchronization using spin van der Pol oscillators as a model. It shows that introducing controlled heterogeneity in the form of coupling mismatches can enhance synchronization, a quantum analog of converse symmetry breaking seen in classical oscillator networks. The authors also vary the spin quantum number to tune the degree of quantumness and examine how quantum effects modify this behavior.

entry.title: Cooling quantum systems with limited resources beyond thermodynamic length
entry.summary: Finite-resource cooling of qudits beyond thermodynamic length arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies cooling a quantum system with N thermal machines, where the cost exceeds Landauer's bound. It shows that for qudits, permutations of energy eigenstates using several resonant transitions at once outperform the thermodynamic-length approach for every spectrum, reducing the excess cost by up to 83% near the ground state. It also finds that coherent collisions do no better at second order, and that at infinite temperature d_M-level machines reduce the excess by at most a factor of d_M-1.

entry.title: Efficient inference of planted k-XOR via hypergraph cycle enumeration
entry.summary: Hypergraph cycle enumeration for efficient inference of planted k-XOR with smooth trade-off arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces hypergraph cycle enumeration (HCE), a simple spectral method for detecting and recovering planted signals in noisy hypergraph inference problems. The authors study it on planted noisy k-XOR, also known as sparse Learning Parity with Noise. HCE achieves recovery performance comparable to the Kikuchi method and outperforms it in some parameter regimes, so neither method is universally better. Replacing one step with a quantum walk gives HCE a subquadratic quantum speedup, which does not refute the quartic quantum speedup of the quantum Kikuchi method.

entry.title: Edge Predictive Maintenance: An Embedded Anomaly Detector Trained with Quantum Optimization
entry.summary: Predictive Maintenance at the Edge: An Embedded Anomaly Detection Pipeline Trained with Quantum Optimization arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents a pipeline that detects bearing anomalies from vibration signals for deployment on low-cost microcontrollers at the edge. It selects vibration features using mRMR with a variational quantum eigensolver, then classifies with a one-class SVM trained by a variational quantum algorithm using Pauli-correlation encoding. In small-scale simulator tests on the Paderborn bearing dataset, the quantum-trained components performed comparably to a classical baseline.

entry.title: Evaluating Antenna Performance with a Quantum Linear System Solver
entry.summary: Finite-Element Electromagnetic Analysis and Evaluation of Antenna Performance Metrics Using a Quantum Linear System Solver arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents a hybrid quantum-classical workflow that combines finite element electromagnetic analysis with a quantum linear system solver to evaluate antenna design metrics. The authors define total radiated power, radiated power within a solid angle, and dielectric and conductive losses as observables that can be computed efficiently from the quantum solution state without reconstructing all its components. Numerical experiments on an axisymmetric coaxially fed monopole antenna under idealized conditions showed relative errors on the order of 10^-3 compared with the classical finite element solution.

entry.title: High-fidelity universal quantum gates in a cryogenic atom array
entry.summary: High-Fidelity Universal Quantum Gates in a Cryogenic Atom Array arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper demonstrates a universal quantum gate set in a cryogenic cesium-133 atom array. Single-qubit gates reach 99.970(2)% fidelity and raw two-qubit entangling gates reach 99.76(8)%, within the range of leading room-temperature implementations. The entangling gate uses direct single-photon coupling to a Rydberg P state, avoiding the scattering and light shifts of two-photon coupling. ★★★★ Notable: The authors demonstrate a universal gate set in a cryogenic cesium atom array, using direct single-photon Rydberg coupling for entangling gates, and report single-qubit fidelity of 99.970(2)% and raw

entry.title: Testing logical Pauli measurements on a trapped-ion computer using QLDPC surgery
entry.summary: Individually Addressed Logical Pauli Measurements by QLDPC Surgery on a Trapped Ion Quantum Computer arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The summary in this language did not pass the date and amount checks, so it is withheld. Check the original.

entry.title: Algebraic strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and partial decodability in the surface code
entry.summary: Algebraic strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and partial decodability in the surface code arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how coherent noise produces unusual regimes of quantum error recovery and mixed-state order. It links a triangular-lattice surface code under single-qubit Z rotations with a Z2 paramagnet under strongly symmetric decoherence through Wegner duality. Increasing the rotation angle leads to a partially decodable critical phase in the code and an algebraic Z2 strong-to-weak symmetry breaking phase in the dual model. The authors derive universal observables using a weakly coupled SO(n) sigma model in the replica limit n→1, and large-scale simulations confirm these predictions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link surface-code decoding and strong-to-weak symmetry breaking via Wegner duality, proposing an algebraic SWSSB phase with universal power-law and fidelity predictions checked numerically

entry.title: Static dipolar impurity in a Fermi gas
entry.summary: Static dipolar impurity in a Fermi gas arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies a static dipolar impurity immersed in a Fermi gas, examining how dipolar interactions shape few-body scattering and the resulting polaron physics. Using Fumi's theorem, the authors link anisotropic phase shifts directly to the ground-state energy and compute the exact impurity spectrum with a functional determinant approach. The spectrum is a convolution of independent even- and odd-wave contributions, yielding a ground state with both even- and odd-wave bound states occupied, whose separation is tunable via the dipole length. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply Fumi's theorem and functional determinants to a dipolar impurity, reporting a doubly occupied ground state that a one-excitation variational ansatz misses.

entry.title: Local determination of low-energy states in weakly interacting gapped fermion systems
entry.summary: Local determination of low-energy states in gapped fermion systems with weak long-range interactions arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies gapped fermion systems obtained by adding sufficiently weak even many-body interactions to a free Hamiltonian with a spectral gap. It proves that if another interaction matches the bulk interaction inside a region U, its low-energy states in the range [0, 3g/4] have local expectations close to the bulk ground state deep inside U, with errors decaying with distance from the complement of U. The results imply, among other things, that the bulk interaction has a unique algebraic ground state. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove quantitative local determination of low-energy states in gapped fermion systems with weak long-range interactions, yielding uniqueness of the algebraic ground state and localization

entry.title: Stability of the bulk gap and spectral flow for fermions with weak long-range interactions
entry.summary: Bulk gap stability and spectral flow for fermions with weak long-range interactions arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proves that weak long-range many-body interactions preserve the bulk gap of a free fermion system. It constructs a quasi-local spectral flow that maps the free ground state to ground states of the interacting system. The results hold under polynomial decay conditions on the coefficients and interactions. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove bulk gap stability and construct a quasi-local spectral flow under weak long-range interactions, with polynomial decay conditions.

entry.title: Three-dimensional quantum cellular automata that cannot be stabilized into circuits
entry.summary: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proves that for every odd prime p, the three-dimensional chiral Z_p Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun, Yang, Wang, Tantivasadakarn and Chen are not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such results were known only within the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a new invariant for invertible subalgebras, proving 3D QCA are not finite-depth circuits beyond the Clifford setting; one key claim remains conjectural.

entry.title: Why the Petz transpose map is the unique quantum analogue of Bayes' rule
entry.summary: Inevitability of the Petz transpose map arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper asks whether quantum theory has a general retrodiction rule analogous to classical Bayes' rule, and whether such a rule is unique. The authors prove that a retrodiction assignment that is involutive, respects sequential and parallel composition, and agrees with unitary inversion must coincide with the Petz transpose map. The result applies to channels between finite-dimensional full matrix algebras. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove Petz transpose map is uniquely forced by consistency axioms, axiomatically characterizing quantum Bayes' rule and a family of doubly rotated maps.

entry.title: Experimental study of a reversible light-induced attack on quantum key distribution transmitters
entry.summary: Reversible photorefractive attack in continuous-variable quantum key distribution arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper experimentally studies a reversible photorefractive attack on a continuous-variable quantum key distribution system. Moderate blue-light illumination lowers the modulation variance of a lithium-niobate IQ modulator to a stable value, and the variance recovers once the light is removed. The authors exploit this recovery to compromise modulation calibration, which leads to overestimated channel transmittance and underestimated excess noise. Key rates computed from the measured parameters can be positive when the correctly calibrated rate is nonpositive. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report a reversible photorefractive attack that exploits recovery to miscalibrate modulation in CV-QKD, turning a nonpositive key rate positive.

entry.title: Non-asymptotic bounds for quantum hypothesis testing via the Nussbaum-Szkoła mapping
entry.summary: Non-Asymptotic Bounds via the Nussbaum-Szkola Mapping for Quantum Hypothesis Testing arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies quantum hypothesis testing, which distinguishes between quantum states. Using the Nussbaum-Szkoła mapping, the authors propose new lower and upper bounds for asymmetric quantum hypothesis testing. These bounds unify converse and achievability results across large-, moderate-, and small-deviation regimes. Numerical comparisons indicate that they approximate the optimal quantum error trade-off function more accurately at small blocklengths. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive unified non-asymptotic lower and upper bounds via the Nussbaum-Szkoła mapping, with numerical comparisons against existing bounds.

entry.title: Optimal Linear Combination of Hamiltonian Simulation for Simulating Dissipative Quantum Dynamics
entry.summary: Optimal Linear Combination of Hamiltonian Simulation for Dissipative Dynamics arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Linear combination of Hamiltonian simulation (LCHS) is an efficient quantum-computing method for simulating dissipative dynamics, and its cost depends on the choice of kernel. The paper proves that the kernel family proposed by Ni and Ying minimizes LCHS query cost in the minimax sense. For target accuracy ε, the minimum cost is asymptotically (2e/π)(ln(1/ε) − ln ln(1/ε) + o(1)), with optimal leading constant 2e/π. The lower-bound proof combines weak duality with a realization lemma. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the Ni-Ying LCHS kernel family is minimax optimal, with leading constant 2e/π, via weak duality and a realization lemma.

entry.title: Composable device-independent quantum digital signatures for verifying message integrity and authenticity
entry.summary: Composable Device-Independent Quantum Digital Signatures arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper establishes a composable security framework for quantum digital signatures within constructive cryptography. It presents a device-independent protocol using one-time universal hashing and multi-channel multiplexing. The authors also derive a related-key security bound for LFSR-based Toeplitz authentication, and numerical simulations indicate efficient signing of multibit documents over metropolitan distances. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build the first composable security framework for QDS, propose a DI-QDS protocol, derive a related-key bound for LFSR-based Toeplitz authentication, and report finite-size simulations.

entry.title: Quantum processes without definite causal order: a limit on how distinguishable and how precisely measurable their outputs can be
entry.summary: Geometric Rényi divergence and RLD Fisher information under quantum processes without definite causal order arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies quantum processes without a definite causal order and proves that the geometric Rényi divergence at the output of a deterministic completely positive process cannot exceed the sum of the divergences of its individual channel uses. It also proves an additive bound on the RLD Fisher information of parameter-dependent channels, which yields a Cramér–Rao bound on locally unbiased estimation precision. An erasure-probability example attains this bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend additive divergence and RLD Fisher information bounds to processes without definite causal order, proving a tight bound, an attaining example, and a Cramér-Rao consequence.

entry.title: High-threshold fusion-based quantum computing with optical hybrid qubits
entry.summary: High-Threshold Fusion-Based Quantum Computation with Optical Hybrid Qubits arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes hybrid fusion-based quantum computation using small optical resource states that combine discrete- and continuous-variable encodings, connected through hybrid fusions. The authors present methods to generate these resource states directly, without local hybrid logic gates, and a decoding strategy that uses error information from individual fusion outcomes. They report a photon loss threshold of 2.231% using 12 hybrid fusions per surface-code unit cell, improving on a previous hybrid measurement-based scheme with a 0.89% threshold and 60 fusions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a hybrid DV-CV fusion-based scheme with a 2.231% loss threshold and 12 fusions per unit cell.

entry.title: From entanglement bootstrap to DHR theory: linking anyon descriptions
entry.summary: From Entanglement Bootstrap to DHR Theory arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper directly connects the entanglement bootstrap with the Doplicher–Haag–Roberts theory of superselection sectors for two-dimensional quantum spin systems. Under the entanglement-bootstrap assumptions, it proves Haag duality and shows a one-to-one correspondence between simple entanglement-bootstrap anyon types and irreducible superselection sectors. For each fusion channel, it constructs an affine bijection between density matrices on the fusion space and normalized positive intertwiners in the operator-algebraic channel. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link entanglement bootstrap to DHR superselection theory, proving Haag duality and a one-to-one anyon-sector correspondence.

entry.title: Classical communication over quantum channels: does entanglement help?
entry.summary: Classical communication over quantum channels: does entanglement help in nature? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether entangling codewords across independent uses of a quantum channel can increase the rate of classical communication. The authors propose a general Schur-weighted block entropy inequality. They show that phase-covariant channels, including multi-level amplitude damping, generalized dephasing, and damping-dephasing channels, have no entanglement advantage. The result also recovers the known conclusion for all qubit channels. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a Schur-weighted block entropy inequality and show no entanglement advantage for phase-covariant channels, recovering the qubit result.

entry.title: What Can Be Computed with Indefinite Causal Structure? A study of whether quantum computing gains power when operations lack a fixed causal order.
entry.summary: What Can Be Computed with Indefinite Causal Structure? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies whether quantum computation becomes more powerful when operations need not follow a definite causal order, using the process matrix formalism of Oreshkov et al. The authors give polynomial-time algorithms in two settings. General process matrices can solve every problem in NP, using valid processes that satisfy the purification postulate and generate unitary channels. Requiring the process matrices to be pure, they solve unique-sink orientation in polynomial time, which suggests indefinite causal order can exceed BQP while preserving unitarity. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show indefinite causal order yields computational power beyond BQP, solving NP problems and unique-sink orientation in polynomial time within the process matrix formalism.

entry.title: On the Quantum Chromatic Gap II: a proof of a strong form of pseudo-telepathy
entry.summary: On the Quantum Chromatic Gap II arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper confirms a conjecture from the first author's SODA'26 paper about Khot's d-to-1 games. It constructs label-cover games with classical value below any given epsilon that still admit a perfect quantum strategy. As a consequence, there are graphs with quantum chromatic number 3 and arbitrarily large classical chromatic number, the first improvement on this gap since Brassard, Cleve, and Tapp. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct graphs with quantum chromatic number 3 and arbitrarily large classical chromatic number, improving on prior exponential gap results.

entry.title: Fast, accurate neural decoding for ultra-high-rate quantum error-correcting codes
entry.summary: Fast and accurate neural triage decoding of ultra-high-rate quantum LDPC codes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces neural triage decoding, a framework that uses syndrome consistency to adaptively allocate neural computation for decoding quantum error-correction codes. A local neural message-passing network quickly predicts corrections, extra iterations reduce residual syndrome violations, and a rarely used diversification stage searches for consistent corrections for the remaining cases. The authors demonstrate the Triage decoder on ultra-high-rate quantum LDPC codes encoding a few hundred logical qubits, including lifted-product and Kasai codes, reporting accuracy comparable to near-optimal algorithmic decoders with latency reduced by roughly one to two orders of magnitude. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a syndrome-consistency-guided neural decoder, reporting near-optimal accuracy with substantially lower latency on high-rate qLDPC codes.

entry.title: Adaptive local measurements can beat fixed global measurements exponentially in quantum learning
entry.summary: Adaptive Local Measurements For Quantum Learning Can Exponentially Outperform Nonadaptive Global Measurements arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper asks whether measurements chosen adaptively, based on earlier outcomes, can be exponentially more informative than measurements fixed in advance. The authors construct multi-qubit states that encode a scalar parameter in one of exponentially many candidate observables, indicated by an auxiliary marker. An adaptive protocol using only single-qubit measurements and one round of adaptation needs logarithmically many copies, while every nonadaptive protocol needs exponentially many. The gap arises from measurement incompatibility, and the states are separable. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that adaptive single-copy local measurements achieve an exponential advantage over nonadaptive global measurements, with tight bounds up to the exponential base.

entry.title: Local quantum fault tolerance without expansion arguments
entry.summary: Local Quantum Fault Tolerance Without Expansion arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies fault-tolerant quantum computation using a fixed local error-correction rule and the cubical (d,d')-Toric code, including the 4D Toric code. Under sufficiently weak local-stochastic Pauli noise, the correction cycle acts only on the current syndrome, has constant depth, and needs no multiscale decoder or scale-dependent delays. The authors give a local higher-dimensional sweep rule, prove a circuit-level threshold theorem for noisy sweep cycles interleaved with logical gates, and bound the probability of ideal decoding under local-stochastic noise. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a local higher-dimensional sweep rule and a circuit-level threshold theorem without expansion, covering the 4D Toric code.

entry.title: Recovering hidden conserved densities in quantum simulators from snapshot measurements
entry.summary: Reconstructing hidden observables via quantum snapshot thermometry arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Projective snapshots on quantum simulators directly probe only observables diagonal in the measurement basis. The paper combines local equilibration with an independently calibrated equilibrium equation of state to reveal hidden conserved-density profiles. Numerical demonstrations show recovery of energy fronts and a diffusion constant, and separation of spin transport from energy spreading.

entry.title: Renormalization for stable memory from independent local updates without synchronization
entry.summary: Renormalization for Robust Memory without Synchronization arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper develops a spacetime renormalization framework showing how independently acting local updates can collectively preserve classical information when sites evolve at random, unsynchronized times. It gives sufficient conditions under which stable interfaces and suppressed defect propagation yield reliable erosion at large scales. Applying this, the authors prove stability of an asynchronous R squeezing code and introduce robust processes in two and three dimensions, where both encoded phases persist under sufficiently weak noise.

entry.title: Comparing entangling strategies for unitary synthesis, a study of how multiqubit gates on trapped-ion computers perform in building target quantum operations.
entry.summary: Comparison of entangling strategies for unitary synthesis arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines whether multiqubit gates on trapped-ion quantum computers are worth their added engineering complexity. The authors use unitary synthesis, a task not tied to any specific application, as a benchmark for gate sets built from native Mølmer–Sørensen multiqubit gates. They also develop a toolset for evaluating such gate sets and identify the hardware requirements under which multiqubit gates become advantageous.

entry.title: Entanglement diagnostics in stochastic-resetting steady states, tested on superconducting qubits
entry.summary: Entanglement diagnostics of stochastic-resetting steady states: theory and measurement on superconducting qubits arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies entanglement in nonequilibrium steady states of the transverse-field Ising chain under stochastic resetting, giving closed-form results for two qubits and exact calculations for chains up to 12 qubits. Measurements on an IBM superconducting processor show averaged entropies closely matching noiseless predictions, while concurrence mostly falls below prediction, captured by a depolarizing model with one fitted parameter. The difference between the two entropies, the Jensen gap, equals the Holevo information a subsystem retains about the time since the last reset, which grows with chain length.</summary>

entry.title: Locality in Dissipative Ground-State Preparation: Whether Local Dissipation Can Prepare a Local Hamiltonian's Ground State
entry.summary: Locality in Dissipative Ground-State Preparation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper asks whether the ground state of a free-fermion Hamiltonian can be prepared using local dissipation. The authors use a quadratic Lindbladian with linear jump operators and link spatial locality to momentum-space analyticity via Fourier correspondence. They derive a complete spectral criterion for exponentially local jump operators that prepare the ground state. The results show that sign-changing Fermi-level crossings rule out such preparation in one dimension, while additional obstructions arise in higher dimensions.

entry.title: Left-handed transmission lines for generating photons via the dynamical Casimir effect
entry.summary: Left-Handed Transmission Lines for the Dynamical Casimir Effect arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies superconducting transmission lines built with series capacitors and shunt inductors, terminated by a flux-modulated SQUID. The authors derive the quantum Hamiltonian and compare the line with a right-handed line and a coplanar waveguide built from the same elements. With equal elements, the left-handed coupling exceeds the right-handed one above a crossover pump frequency, and the created particles stay in the target mode.

entry.title: Optimal estimation of diamond distance between unitary channels
entry.summary: Optimal Diamond Distance Estimation for Unitary Channels arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents a quantum algorithm that estimates the diamond distance between two unknown d-dimensional unitary channels to within additive error ε. It uses O(√d/ε) queries to the unitary channels and their inverses. The query complexity matches the lower bound due to Jeon and Oh (npj Quantum Inf., 2026), so the algorithm is optimal.

entry.title: Using Exceptional Points to Detect Non-Gaussian Noise
entry.summary: Exceptional Points as Witnesses of Non-Gaussian Noise arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper shows that exceptional points (EPs) in the noise-averaged dephasing response of quantum devices can reveal non-Gaussian noise statistics that the power spectrum alone cannot distinguish. It introduces a model describing dephasing environments as identical independent noise sources while preserving the power spectrum. Given a calibrated single-source model, the largest EP order extracted from the measured response determines the number of sources and predicts higher-order statistics of the combined noise.

entry.title: Algebraic theory of abelian fractons: fusion, mobility and statistics in gapped fracton phases
entry.summary: Algebraic theory of abelian fractons and beyond arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper develops an algebraic framework for fusion, mobility and statistics in abelian gapped fracton orders and topological phases, generalizing the algebraic description of abelian anyons to systems with restricted mobility and extended excitations. It introduces braided fusion complexes, which encode fusion, mobility and statistics, and defines braided fusion theories as their equivalence classes. The authors also study mutual statistics and remote detection for nondegenerate theories, and prove that the excitation-detector principle is equivalent to nondegeneracy under a unique infinite-space ground state assumption.

entry.title: Optimal detuning and gate time for strong single-qubit gates beyond the rotating-wave approximation
entry.summary: Optimal detuning and gate time for strongly driven single-qubit gates beyond the rotating-wave approximation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how single-qubit quantum gates lose accuracy when strong driving is used, since the rotating-wave approximation no longer holds. The authors analyse the error using an effective Magnus-Taylor Hamiltonian through second order in the inverse driving frequency. They correct the driving frequency with an amplitude-dependent Bloch-Siegert-type shift and rescale the gate time to restore the RWA gate conditions. Numerical solutions of the Schrödinger equation show that these corrections reduce gate infidelity by several orders of magnitude, widening the usable range of driving amplitudes.

entry.title: Probing photon emission fluctuations in spin-injected quantum dots using time-dependent electrical excitation
entry.summary: Probing fluctuations in photon emission statistics of spin injected quantum dots with time dependent electronic excitation arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies electrically spin-injected InGaAs/GaAs quantum dot ensembles that emit circularly polarized single photons without an external pump laser. Using an extended Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometer with four detectors, the authors measure time-resolved photon-number statistics and find that two-photon statistics fluctuate at several points within each excitation pulse. These fluctuations disappear when the spin-injection layer is demagnetized, linking multi-photon emission dynamics to the spin polarization of injected carriers.

entry.title: Nested toric codes: decoupling translation-invariant topological CSS codes in higher dimensions
entry.summary: Toric codes all the way down: decoupling translation-invariant topological CSS codes in higher dimensions arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies topological CSS quantum error-correcting codes in three or more spatial dimensions, which are useful for fault-tolerant quantum computation. The authors show that such a code can be decoupled into a stack of higher-form toric codes by a finite-depth local Clifford circuit once, after coarse-graining to a superlattice, translations act trivially on each excitation layer and the gluing between layers vanishes. They also give an explicit algorithm that builds this decoupling circuit from SUM and SWAP gates.

entry.title: Grow, Compress, and Perturb: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Method for Scalable Quantum Chemistry
entry.summary: Grow, Compress, and Perturb: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Pathway to Scalable Quantum Chemistry on Quantum Computers arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces VULCAN, a layered variational quantum eigensolver framework that avoids Hamiltonian gradient measurements by building ansatz operators dynamically with variational double bracket flow. Emulations on up to 32 logical qubits reach chemical accuracy for hydrogen chains, BeH2, and H2O using 5-20% of the measurement cost of batched ADAPT-VQE. For the 32-qubit C3H6 case, a single VULCAN layer combined with a GPU-accelerated stochastic ENPT2 correction reaches chemical accuracy, where batched ADAPT-VQE does not.

entry.title: Quasi-Phases of Quantum Matter: Distinct Gapped Regimes Near a Critical Point
entry.summary: Quasi-Phases of Quantum Matter arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces quasi-phases, gapped regimes near a critical point that are connected in the broader phase diagram but not by any gapped path reachable through small perturbations of the critical theory. In spin-chain examples with central charge c=1, the authors identify multicritical c=3/2 and c=9/5 orbifolds that describe these quasi-phases. The work also argues that such quasi-phases can carry interface modes with higher-dimensional linear representations.

entry.title: Gauge-invariant orbital angular momentum of vector optical vortices beyond the paraxial approximation
entry.summary: On the gauge-invariant orbital angular momentum of vector optical vortices in the paraxial approximation and beyond arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents a gauge-invariant formalism for describing the spin and orbital angular momenta of scalar and vector optical vortices. A correction term arising from consistent treatment of the transverse vector potential's nonlocality restores gauge invariance and allows the total angular momentum to be separated into spin and orbital parts. The authors show that the orbital angular momentum of multimode vector vortex beams has two qualitatively different components and discuss the limits of applicability of the formalism.

entry.title: Benchmarking fast quantum annealing with domain walls
entry.summary: Using domain walls to benchmark fast quantum anneals arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies the distribution of domain walls in ground states of frustrated one-dimensional Ising spin chains with anti-parallel boundary spins. Ideal chains are expected to show a sine-squared distribution quantumly and a uniform distribution classically, while chains with random imperfections on a physical device show a U-shaped profile. Using D-Wave's fast anneal feature, the authors observe a sine-squared distribution consistent with coherent quantum behavior and propose the extent of the domain wall distribution tail as a platform-independent metric.

entry.title: Lattice moments and quantum designs
entry.summary: Lattice moments and quantum designs arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper shows that the ensemble of unimodular Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill distributions does not form a rigged quantum 3-design. It quantifies the replica defect responsible for this failure. The result is established by rederiving a second moment formula for symplectic lattices in a self-contained way.

entry.title: Entropic fluctuations in quantum statistical mechanics: a review of how classical entropy fluctuation theorems are extended to quantum systems.
entry.summary: Entropic Fluctuations in Quantum Statistical Mechanics: A Review arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper reviews and compares several ways the Evans-Searles and Gallavotti-Cohen fluctuation theorems for entropy production can be extended to quantum systems. It introduces a recent approach and adds an extension of the steady-state version to two-time measurement entropy production in the algebraic setting. The authors discuss open quantum systems, the connection to modular theory, and a quantum principle of regular entropic fluctuations. They also relate these entropy production statistics to spectral resonances of quantum transfer operators, applied to the spin-fermion model.

entry.title: Spectral metrics inspired by quantum walks for judging QAOA mixer choices
entry.summary: Quantum-Walk Inspired Spectral Metrics for Evaluating QAOA Mixers arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Inspired by quantum-walk mixing theory, the paper proposes two spectral indicators for QAOA mixer topologies: the normalized minimum eigenvalue separation of the mixer Hamiltonian, and the long-time averaged minimum eigenvalue separation of the mixer unitary. The authors derive exact expressions and asymptotic bounds for the complete graph, hypercube, cycle, and balanced 2-D torus. For random permutation-invariant cost Hamiltonians the spectral ordering broadly matches observed QAOA performance, but for structured 1-D and 2-D Ising QUBOs it breaks down, suggesting mixer-cost alignment matters.

entry.title: Sharpening particle trajectories by changing quantum reference frames
entry.summary: Trajectory sharpening under quantum reference frame transformations arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper links quantum reference frame transformations to experimental effects. Using a toy model of free particles with signed masses, it shows that trajectory sharpening from correlating a system with a negative-mass reference can be read as a transformation to a negative-mass frame. The authors define frame-invariant sharpness measures and derive monogamy relations limiting sharpness with respect to two negative-mass frames.

entry.title: Process matrices for generalised physical theories, extending indefinite causal order beyond quantum theory.
entry.summary: Process matrices on generalised theories arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper extends the process-matrix framework for indefinite causal orders to a broad class of generalised physical theories. It re-axiomatises spacetime contexts through naturality over classical probes, capturing non-contextual assignment with compatibility for convexity and coarse-graining. It characterises which theories admit a process-matrix representation of abstract spacetime contexts, and identifies when supermap and process-matrix perspectives coincide in classical, quantum, and Boxworld-like theories.

entry.title: A universal gauge structure in the photon content of light-matter systems
entry.summary: A universal gauge structure in the photon content of light-matter systems arXiv · Oct 30, 2026After truncating the matter space of single-mode light-matter models, gauge changes leave the spectrum unchanged but alter the ground-state photon number, whose meaning has been disputed. The paper shows that when the gauge transformation is a field displacement coupled to a matter operator, this photon number is an exact quadratic polynomial in the gauge parameter. Its minimum over all gauges is gauge-invariant and, for the quantum Rabi model, is set by the ground-state energy alone.

entry.title: Structural limits of QAOA mixer design: transport and causal reach
entry.summary: Structural Bottlenecks in QAOA Mixer Design: Transport and Causal Reach arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper examines mixer design in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), identifying two structural bottlenecks for shallow circuits: probability transport across configuration space and finite-depth causal reach. It derives mixer-dependent first-order objective bounds and a non-perturbative spreading condition. For MaxCut, it adds problem-graph-aligned two-local interactions to the transverse-field mixer, and reports that X+XX and X+YY improve approximation ratios over the standard X mixer at equal depth.

entry.title: Electric field control of spin transport anisotropy in a layered antiferromagnet
entry.summary: Electric field control of anisotropic spin traffic between spin-filtering and magnon-scattering in a layered antiferromagnet arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies a dual-gate field-effect transistor built on CrSBr, a layered A-type antiferromagnetic semiconductor. The measurements show that the displacement field, rather than carrier doping, mainly determines the sign and magnitude of the magnetoresistance ratio. The authors explain the effect using ab initio calculations and an effective spin-circuit model. They conclude that the displacement field is an efficient electrical knob for controlling spin transport in CrSBr.

entry.title: Micromagnetic Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulation of magnon-photon coupling in cavities
entry.summary: Micromagnetic Lagrangian and Hamiltonian Normal-Mode Formulation of Cavity Magnon-Photon Interactions arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how magnons and photons interact inside a resonant microwave cavity, starting from linearized Maxwell and Landau-Lifshitz equations. The authors introduce an electric vector potential and an interaction Lagrangian, expand fields in normal modes, and derive a Hamiltonian using the Faddeev-Jackiw approach. A generalized Bogoliubov transformation then diagonalizes the coupled system into polariton variables. As an example, a perpendicularly magnetized YIG disk in a rectangular cavity shows hybridization of the cavity mode with several magnetostatic modes and frequency shifts near conducting walls.

entry.title: Fault-tolerant Heisenberg-limited quantum sensing using bosonic probes
entry.summary: Fault-Tolerant Heisenberg-Limited Quantum Metrology with Bosonic Probes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes a fault-tolerant protocol that uses bosonic probes to estimate displacements in the presence of dephasing noise. The authors construct an optimal error-correcting code under a mean photon-number constraint, with a repetition-encoded qubit register and repeated boson-parity measurements. Under circuit-level bit-flip noise, a distance-d code suppresses logical failures to order p^((d+1)/2). The Fisher information scales as NT² over interrogation times of order γ_A^(-(d+1)/2), compared with γ_A^(-1) for the non-fault-tolerant approach.

entry.title: Classifying cavity-modified reaction types via linear free-energy relationships
entry.summary: Characterizing Reaction Types through Linear Free-Energy Relationships in Cavities arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper extends nonempirical linear free-energy relationships to reactions inside optical cavities and finds that they fall into four reaction types set by simple response-crossing rules. Reactions may follow conventional Bell-Evans-Polanyi (BEP) or counterintuitive Opposite-BEP behavior, or switch between them as cavity frequency changes. The framework is demonstrated in the Shin-Metiu model and four molecular reactions, and the complexity is reduced to competition between permanent-dipole and polarizability responses.

entry.title: Quantum computing via computational imaging: representation, measurement, and inference
entry.summary: Quantum Computing through Computational Imaging: Representations, Measurement, and Inference arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper, aimed at computational-imaging and engineering readers, examines how the representation, measurement, and decoding of a quantum state determine what information can be returned. It distinguishes amplitude encodings of input values from encodings of complete candidate labelings, and studies unknown-phase inference under complex-field interference. It links singular-value decomposition of reshaped joint amplitudes to pure-state entanglement. In a four-pixel segmentation example, one QAOA layer lowers mean energy relative to uniform sampling yet makes a nonoptimal labeling more probable than the optimum.

entry.title: Fast mixing of Gibbs samplers for quantum spin systems with all-to-all coupling
entry.summary: Rapid mixing for Gibbs samplers for quantum spin systems with all-to-all interactions arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how quickly Gibbs states of two-local quantum Hamiltonians on arbitrary interaction graphs, including fully connected systems, can be prepared using Lindblad dynamics satisfying KMS detailed balance. The authors adapt the classical Dobrushin condition to the quantum setting and use the order-1 quantum Wasserstein distance to measure how local perturbations spread. In a high-temperature regime set by the maximum total interaction strength per site, they derive contraction estimates that yield mixing times logarithmic in system size and inverse error tolerance.

entry.title: Subsystem Spacetime Code: A Quantum Error-Correction Framework for Measuring Clifford Circuit Fault Distance
entry.summary: Subsystem Spacetime Code arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper constructs a subsystem spacetime code and uses it to characterize the distances of Clifford circuits. Its gauge group can be explicitly constructed and classified using masking properties of instantaneous stabilizer groups, and consists of faults that are harmless to the circuit. The framework is also used to identify where a dynamical code loses distance and to analyze how fault distance changes when circuits are composed from smaller components.

entry.title: Multidimensional Revival Dynamics in a Bosonic Many-Body System: A study of how localized quantum states collapse and revive in a two-site Bose-Hubbard model
entry.summary: Multidimensional revival dynamics in a bosonic many-body system arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies quantum interference in a symmetric two-site Bose-Hubbard model. Starting from a coherent state prepared on one site in the strongly self-trapping regime, the authors derive revival behaviors in expectation values, coherences, and the autocorrelation function, and illustrate the entanglement behavior. They identify several new features and show that a comprehensive semiclassical theory explains them, with excellent agreement to quantitative comparisons.

entry.title: QDMin: Quantum Search for Energy Minima in Nuclear Shape Landscapes
entry.summary: QDMin: Coherent Quantum Minimum Finding for Nuclear Deformation Landscapes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents QDMin, a method for locating the minimum of a nuclear collective energy landscape. It searches a parameterized Hamiltonian family using a coherent collective-coordinate register and an on-demand ground-energy threshold oracle, avoiding point-by-point construction of the landscape. The method is implemented for a schematic pairing-plus-multipole model, with calculations at four points and on a 4×4 quadrupole–octupole grid.

entry.title: Transport in spinful non-Hermitian gauge lattices: spin-dependent skin effects and transmission in one-dimensional lattices with gauge fields
entry.summary: Transport in spinful non-Hermitian gauge lattices arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper extends a generalized transfer-matrix method to one-dimensional non-Hermitian tight-binding lattices with spin and matrix-valued Abelian and non-Abelian gauge couplings. In the Abelian case the spin sectors separate, giving exact spectra and closed transport expressions with spin-dependent skin localization. In the non-Abelian case noncommuting couplings mix the spin sectors, producing spin-hybridized lasing, coherent perfect absorption, and direction-dependent reflectionless transport with spin conversion.

entry.title: Upper bounds on general (r,δ) quantum locally recoverable codes
entry.summary: Bounds for General (r,δ)-Quantum Locally Recoverable Codes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies general (r,δ) quantum locally recoverable codes without assuming purity or stabilizer structure, allowing recovery blocks to overlap arbitrarily. It establishes a Singleton-like upper bound for general quantum subspaces and tightens it with an explicit remainder correction. The authors also extend a known pure-code parameter bound to arbitrary pure quantum subspaces and analyze three code families that attain these bounds.

entry.title: Stabilizing fluctuating Cooper pairs using a terahertz resonator
entry.summary: Stabilizing fluctuating Cooper pairs with a terahertz resonator arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper develops an equilibrium theory of a mesoscopic, disordered two-dimensional superconductor coupled to a subwavelength terahertz resonator, focusing on how superconducting phase fluctuations interact with the resonator's electromagnetic fluctuations. Modeling the resonator as a lumped-element circuit, the authors find that coupling raises the superconducting transition temperature Tc rather than suppressing it. For a 1 µm × 1 µm, 8 nm-thick disordered film, they estimate a relative Tc enhancement of about 1%, roughly ten times the 0.1% obtained when phase fluctuations are neglected.

entry.title: Detuned cavity boosts spectroscopy precision for dipole moment estimation
entry.summary: Detuning-assisted cavity enhancement in spectroscopy arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies cavity-enhanced spectroscopy with the cavity frequency deliberately detuned from the transition of interest. The authors report that detuning can improve dipole moment estimation precision by up to two orders of magnitude compared with resonant operation, including in the presence of losses. They attribute the gain to a detuning-controlled redistribution of information between light- and matter-like polaritons, and note it is accessible with conventional photodetection and time-correlated single-photon counting.

entry.title: A density calculus for quantum field theory: an introduction to Haagerup L^p spaces
entry.summary: A density calculus for quantum field theory arXiv · Oct 29, 2026These notes introduce Haagerup noncommutative L^p spaces for quantum field theorists, extending density matrix calculus to type III algebras where no intrinsic trace exists. The authors construct the spaces first for matrices, via crossed products and dual actions, then for general von Neumann algebras, discussing how normal states are represented by Haagerup densities. As an application, they compute the sandwiched Rényi divergence for a coherent excitation of a chiral current, checking monotonicity under restriction and the Rényi quantum null energy condition for all real orders α>1.

entry.title: Estimating how alike two unknown continuous-variable quantum states are, across separate quantum platforms
entry.summary: Distributed Inner-Product Estimation for Continuous-Variable Quantum States arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes a CV-DIPE protocol that estimates the inner product between two unknown quantum states prepared on distributed platforms. It uses only local homodyne measurements at shared phase settings and classical communication. Under a known bound on mean energy per mode, the authors derive explicit finite-sample guarantees and sufficient copy counts for a prescribed accuracy and confidence. Numerical simulations with Gaussian and non-Gaussian states show the trade-off between truncation bias and statistical error.

entry.title: A dissipative controller as a hidden source of quantum gate errors
entry.summary: Dissipative controller as a hidden source of errors in quantum gates arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Quantum systems are usually controlled by classical devices that inevitably dissipate energy into their surroundings. Using the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, the paper studies how the noise in the control field relates to the entropy produced by the macroscopic controller, working with a minimal model. In the fast-control, high-fidelity regime, it finds a tradeoff between dissipation and control errors. Perturbative calculations of gate fidelity and of state-transfer fidelity via shortcuts to adiabaticity in the Landau-Zener model illustrate this tradeoff.

entry.title: Identifying Executed Logical Operations from Syndrome Histories in qLDPC Codes
entry.summary: Identifying Logical Operations from Syndrome Histories for qLDPC Codes arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper shows that syndrome histories, normally used for error correction in fault-tolerant quantum computation, can also reveal which logical operations were executed. The authors develop an exact inference method and a scalable approximation that account for unknown faults and measurement randomness. Evaluated on [[18,4,2]] and [[72,12,6]] bivariate bicycle codes, single logical instructions are identified with over 94% accuracy under circuit-level noise.

entry.title: Non-Bloch dynamical quantum phase transitions in chains with memory
entry.summary: Non-Bloch Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions with Memory arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Dynamical quantum phase transitions in periodic chains are governed by real Bloch momenta. This paper identifies non-Bloch transitions that appear only in open chains and are governed by complex momenta, arising in a Hermitian chain coupled to a simple substrate with exactly treated memory. The effect stems from the point-gap winding number W of the projected propagator. For nonzero W, open boundaries alter both the dynamical free energy and critical times, even in the thermodynamic limit, and both follow from analytic continuation to complex momenta. The authors also show that W can be measured by particle counting.

entry.title: Nonequilibrium thermodynamics of a small quantum system linked to quantum heat reservoirs
entry.summary: Nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics of a small quantum system coupled to quantum reservoirs arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper uses a statistical mechanical framework in which nonequilibrium averages of selected quantum observables are expressed exactly as averages over local density operators, to describe a small quantum system coupled to reservoirs. It focuses on how the system's average internal energy evolves, including under external autonomous driving that does work on it, and on entropy production within the system. When the system couples to large quantum reservoirs, its effect on them is captured by boundary conditions on the reservoir equations, which the authors derive. The framework is illustrated with heat transfer through a quantum system connected to two heat reservoirs at different temperatures.

entry.title: Whether a quantum system's memory measures depend on its surrounding environment's state
entry.summary: Bath-state (In)dependence of Non-Markovianity Measures in Quadratic Open Systems arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies a fermionic quadratic open quantum system. It shows that the Breuer-Laine-Piilo and Lorenzo-Plastina-Paternostro non-Markovianity measures are independent of the bath state. In contrast, the Rivas-Huelga-Plenio measures and the Megier-Smirne-Vacchini entropic measure remain sensitive to the reservoir's temperature and chemical potential.

entry.title: Kelvin-wave multiplication through sound emission
entry.summary: Kelvin-Wave Multiplication by Sound Emission arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies how a subsonic Kelvin quantum can emit a phonon and split into two lower-energy quanta, increasing Kelvin population while losing energy. In the soft-phonon limit, rotational invariance links the leading acoustic shear amplitude to the released energy, and microscopic calculations support this dispersion dependence. In a reflecting cavity with coherent sound and Kelvin seeds, Gross-Pitaevskii simulations show Kelvin gain, and shifting the initial sound phase by π reverses these changes.

entry.title: Quantum neural network combining digital and analog operations using long-range interactions
entry.summary: Digital-Analog Quantum Neural Network with Long-Range Interactions arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper proposes a digital-analog quantum neural network (DA-QNN) whose analog blocks use an Ising model with power-law long-range interactions to generate entanglement, reducing the number of two-qubit entangling gates. It is benchmarked on supervised and unsupervised learning tasks. For image classification and many-body phase detection, the long-range ansatz matches short-range performance with fewer layers or shorter evolution times. In unsupervised phase detection, the two ansatzes give complementary signatures that together reconstruct the full phase diagram.

entry.title: Entropy-maximizing mixed quantum states with a fixed average
entry.summary: Maximum-Entropy Ensemble of Quantum Subsystems with a Fixed Average State arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies the maximum-entropy distribution of mixed quantum states under a fixed ensemble average. Its eigenvalue density is argued to converge asymptotically to that of the correlated Wishart ensemble (CWE), obtained via a free multiplicative convolution formula. Applied to the transverse-field Ising model with a thermal average state, it yields a high-temperature correction to the Marchenko-Pastur law. The authors also show, with numerical support, that the ensemble after random POVM measurement is asymptotically equivalent to the CWE, and compute finite-temperature Page curves for average entanglement entropy.

entry.title: Optimized dynamical decoupling for spin ensembles with large inhomogeneities
entry.summary: Optimized Dynamical Decoupling for Spin Ensembles with Large Inhomogeneities arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper compares many dynamical decoupling (DD) protocols for protecting coherence and enabling quantum sensing in an ensemble of negatively charged NV centers in diamond under ambient conditions. The authors identify an optimal approach that uses rapid adiabatic passage pulses, which are robust to amplitude and frequency inhomogeneity, combined with varying their phases. Experiments show improved signal contrast and an order-of-magnitude longer memory time compared to XY8 with standard rectangular pulses, and the method is also applied to sensing a weak oscillating field.

entry.title: Error-Corrected Quantum Optimization with Rydberg Atom Array Embeddings: Using Embedding Ancillary Atoms for Error Correction
entry.summary: Error-Corrected Quantum Optimization via Rydberg Atom Array Embeddings arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies how Rydberg atom arrays solve combinatorial optimization on complex graphs through embeddings that add ancillary atoms. The authors show that the embedding structure naturally forms a classical error-correcting code and introduce a Cluster decoder to correct bit-flip errors. On the QuEra Aquila device, the decoder recovered exact optimization solutions with an average success rate of at least 8% for systems of up to 107 atoms.

entry.title: A method for detecting and suppressing quantum decoherence caused by collisions with the environment.
entry.summary: Detection and Inhibition of Decoherence Through Collisions: A dynamical approach arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper proposes two protocols for protecting quantum states from noise without needing full knowledge of the noise dynamics, based on a collisional model. The first preserves the states of qubits, and the second protects a logical qubit under similar conditions. According to the paper, the protocols protect arbitrary single-qubit and entangled states against general noise and scale to any number of qubits.

entry.title: Probabilistic imaginary-time evolution using precompiled diagonal Hamiltonian representations
entry.summary: Probabilistic imaginary-time evolution via compiled diagonal representations arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper proposes a probabilistic imaginary-time evolution method that uses a compiled approximate diagonal representation of the Hamiltonian, with the basis transformation optimized offline. For a fixed compiled representation, the online circuit structure and gate count per attempt do not depend on imaginary time, and the representation can be reused across input states and evolution times. The authors derive a condition for enhanced success probability and report numerical tests showing lower online cost than termwise Pauli-based methods at a common accuracy threshold. They also examine how approximation errors and offline preparation costs affect the overall benefit.

entry.title: Sharp Tilting Inequalities: An Optimal Bound on the Directional Derivative of the Logarithm and Fractional Powers
entry.summary: Sharp Tilting Inequalities arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies a trace inequality for positive semidefinite matrices A and B, involving the directional derivative of the logarithm and fractional powers, with parameter 1/2≤α≤1. The authors prove an upper bound with the optimal coefficient. The result extends to positive trace-class A and positive, possibly unbounded, self-adjoint B on a separable Hilbert space. The proof uses a superoperator representation of the logarithm's directional derivative and an Araki-type estimate for the derivative of a fractional power.

entry.title: Training quantum algorithms with adiabatic methods to detect entanglement
entry.summary: Adiabatic training of VQAs for entanglement detection arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes a hybrid quantum framework that trains Variational Quantum Algorithms with an adiabatic-inspired optimization strategy to detect entanglement. The method combines parameter-space discretization with a hierarchical segmentation scheme and formulates the problem as a QUBO model for quantum annealing. Preliminary results are compared against classical neural networks and conventional VQA training techniques.

entry.title: Pöschl-Teller-type Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonians via supersymmetric transformations
entry.summary: Pöschl-Teller type of Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonians: SUSY transformations arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper uses supersymmetric quantum mechanics to define and study generalized Jaynes-Cummings (JC) Hamiltonians. Trigonometric and hyperbolic Pöschl-Teller potentials are used to modify the standard JC model. The generalized Hamiltonians share several features with the standard JC model, including matrix intertwining, excitation number symmetry, Rabi frequency, atomic inversion formulas, and classical and revival times. The authors conclude that the JC Hamiltonian is one example of a wider class of generalized Hamiltonians.

entry.title: Conditional Information Flow in Rotated Cluster States and Neural Learnability
entry.summary: Conditional Information Flow and Neural Representability of One-Dimensional Rotated Cluster States arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies how measurement outcomes in one-dimensional rotated cluster states stay conditionally dependent over long distances, despite an exact matrix product state bond dimension of 2. It compares the conditional mutual information of an entanglement-swapping endpoint readout with a bulk readout of the locally equivalent conventional cluster state, using the spin-1 AKLT chain as an exact control. The paper also benchmarks several neural learners on the same target, finding that building the small virtual memory into the architecture greatly eases optimization.

entry.title: Closed-form solutions for fully quantized parametric amplification
entry.summary: Analytic Solutions To Fully Quantized Parametric Amplification arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper derives analytic expressions for how observables evolve under the fully quantized trilinear Hamiltonian that describes quantum three-wave mixing and parametric amplification. Starting from a coherent pump and vacuum signal and idler, the authors reorganize the Heisenberg expansion into resummed depletion and return profiles, giving directly evaluable expressions for correlations up to third order. Numerical benchmarks reported in the paper show errors around 10^-12 across the full pump depletion and below 10^-3 over dozens of depletion-and-back-conversion cycles.

entry.title: Efficient experimental classification of quantum data using quantum kernels
entry.summary: Provably efficient experimental classification of quantum data with quantum kernels arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper proposes a framework for efficient quantum-state classification that reduces the number of measurements needed, deriving conditions under which the measurement count grows polynomially with system size. It applies this to classifying stellar rank, a measure of non-Gaussianity, in continuous-variable quantum computing. The authors experimentally classify single-mode states with stellar rank zero and one on a programmable photonic processor, reporting accurate results despite experimental imperfections.

entry.title: A family of fermionic relative Rényi negativities in Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev models
entry.summary: A Zoo of Fermionic Relative Rényi Negativities in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Models arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces relative Rényi negativities as entanglement witnesses for mixed fermionic states. The authors relate fermionic partial time reversal to the size superoperator to obtain a path-integral representation. They evaluate these quantities in thermal states of the SYK model and the Maldacena-Qi coupled SYK model using a large-N expansion. The study identifies a class that plausibly approximates logarithmic negativity and finds first-order entanglement transitions not visible in simple observables.

entry.title: NAKO: A Benchmark for Testing and Diagnosing Compilers for Neutral-Atom Quantum Computers
entry.summary: NAKO: A Benchmarking Framework for Evaluating and Diagnosing Neutral-Atom Quantum Compilers arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Neutral-atom quantum processors must jointly schedule gates, place atoms, and move them in parallel, so compiler choices drive physical costs. This paper introduces NAKO, a benchmarking framework that pairs each benchmark with an executable reference schedule to measure resource gaps in compiler outputs. Controlled interventions on reference mappings and intermediate states trace excess costs to specific compiler decisions. In a 648-run evaluation of Enola and OLSQ-DPQA, NAKO identifies distinct bottlenecks in each compiler and validates resource savings from targeted fixes.

entry.title: Quantum field theory with scale-dependent weighted measures in momentum space
entry.summary: Quantum field theory with scale-dependent weighted measures: nonlinear momentum representations, vacuum fluctuations, and causal structure arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper revisits constructing free quantum fields using weighted measures in momentum space, adding an independent energy scale that recovers the conventional theory at low momenta. The resulting family is described by a dimensionless spectral function, with the spatial weight linked to the Euclidean Snyder algebra as one special case. It also examines connections to modified dispersion relations and nonlinear momentum coordinates, and analyzes equal-time algebra, vacuum fluctuations, two-point functions and nonlocal causal structure for the complex Klein-Gordon field.

entry.title: Dissipation dilution boosts SiV coupling to diamond nanomechanical beams
entry.summary: Dissipation dilution enhances SiV coupling to vdW diamond nanomechanics arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper experimentally studies a tensioned diamond nanobeam platform where strain couples negatively charged silicon vacancy centers to a mechanical resonator. By monitoring the SiVs' optical response, the authors observe that dynamical strain localizes near the clamps under static strain. This enhances both SiV-mechanical coupling and mechanical coherence, and yields a strain sensitivity with much better accuracy than prior literature values.

entry.title: Quantum Optimization Using Cavity Dissipation to Escape Local Minima
entry.summary: Efficient Quantum Optimization via Dissipative False Vacuum Decay arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes a cavity-based dissipative quantum solver for a class of NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems encoded as atomic-spin Hamiltonians. The method uses dissipative false-vacuum decay in configuration space to escape metastable local minima in rugged energy landscapes. Numerical studies on MaxCut and Maximum Independent Set identify favorable parameter regions, and time complexity estimates based on finite-size scaling are reported as more favorable than standard Grover search.

entry.title: A design and verification flow for quantum circuits modeled on VLSI practice, tested on pi estimation
entry.summary: A VLSI-Like Design and Verification Flow for Quantum Circuits: A Case Study in PI Estimation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes a four-level design and verification flow for quantum circuits, adapted from conventional VLSI digital design, covering behavioral modeling, register-transfer level, gate level, and integration with quantum algorithms. It uses quantum Monte Carlo pi estimation as a case study to show a path from specifications to large-scale circuit implementation. Classical simulations indicate that replacing random sampling with grid sampling yields a quadratic improvement in this case without any quantum computation, suggesting the speedup may come from the sampling strategy rather than the quantum amplitude estimation circuit.

entry.title: Beyond Direct Imaging: Quantum Measurement Design for Small-Target Detection in UAV Hyperspectral Sensing
entry.summary: Beyond Direct Imaging: Quantum Measurement Design for Small-Target Detection in UAV Hyperspectral Sensing arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper proposes a quantum-assisted framework for detecting small targets in UAV hyperspectral sensing by comparing direct imaging with spatial-mode measurements. Simulations based on measured mineral spectra and published UAV acquisition scales, at a shared active-exposure budget, show it outperforms complete direct imaging. At an empirical 1% region-level false alarm rate, detection for a representative target rises from 62.95% to 69.65%.

entry.title: Spatial-mode selection for measuring mineral absorption in small regions
entry.summary: Spatial-Mode Selection for Local Mineral Absorption Spectroscopy arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes a quantum-inspired measurement framework that uses spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) to keep the absorption response of a small mineral region while reducing background light before detection. In equal-time simulations that include localization uncertainty, alignment time, calibration, and detector costs, it reduces absorption-depth root-mean-square error by 14% to 26% across five absorption strengths compared with all-pixel direct imaging using the same background freedom.

entry.title: Force sensing in a recoverable bosonic quantum memory, a paper on sensing an external force while protecting quantum information
entry.summary: Force Sensing in a Recoverable Bosonic Quantum Memory arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper constructs finite-energy bosonic codes that let a single oscillator sense an external force while actively protecting an unknown logical qubit. Logical amplitudes are encoded across discrete wave-packet sites, and the force signal is captured in a shared internal coordinate, enabling a probe readout independent of the logical state under continuous photon loss. Binomial site recovery is shown to suppress memory infidelity and memory-probe correlations at stated orders, and superconducting circuit benchmarks identify preferred encoding regimes for hardware.

entry.title: Competition Between Resonance and Transition Channels in Cavity-Assisted Floquet-State Stabilization
entry.summary: Resonance and Transition-Channel Competition in Cavity-Assisted Floquet-State Stabilization arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies coupling a driven quantum system to a dissipative cavity to autonomously stabilize Floquet eigenstates. At intermediate driving frequencies, meeting the resonance condition alone is shown to be insufficient, because the steady state depends on the interplay between resonance selection and cavity-induced transition strengths. This interplay can yield successful stabilization, mixed steady states despite resonance, or complete breakdown near Floquet-zone hybridization. The authors state that the same mechanism extends to multilevel spin-S systems.

entry.title: Narrowband and ultrashort-pulse-like probing in CARS using twin beams and SFG readout
entry.summary: Signatures of Narrowband and Ultrashort-Pulse-Like Probing in Coherent Anti-Stokes Raman Scattering Using Twin Beams and Sum-Frequency Generation Readout arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper theoretically studies coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS) driven by bright twin beams, with sum-frequency generation (SFG) as the readout. Expressing the SFG output through quantum-field correlation functions reveals several correlation structures tied to different interaction pathways on the bra and ket sides. Frequency correlations between the CARS probe and SFG gating fields let the two fields act together as an effective narrowband probe, avoiding probe-induced spectral convolution.

entry.title: Beyond energy bounds: comparing Schrödinger eigenstates
entry.summary: Beyond energy bounds: comparing Schrödinger eigenstates arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper derives comparisons between eigenstates of ordered Schrödinger operators, extending energy bounds to ground-state overlaps, spatial distributions and nodes. In one dimension and radially, a single crossing condition on the potential difference orders ground-state likelihood ratios and monotone observables. For Yukawa ground states, Hulthén comparison functions bound overlaps, radial moments and the density at the nucleus, yielding a lower bound of about 1.13611 on the scaled critical screening parameter.

entry.title: Reverse quantum annealing to compute molecular ground-state energies
entry.summary: Reverse Quantum Annealing for Ground-State Energy Calculation in Molecule arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper reports reverse quantum annealing calculations of ground-state energies for alkaline-earth monofluoride molecules. The Dirac-Coulomb electronic Hamiltonian is split into sub-QUBOs, and forward-annealing solutions are refined with optimized reverse-annealing schedules to systematically reduce residual configuration errors. Electronic ground-state wave functions and energies are obtained with the Quantum Annealing Eigensolver algorithm, and the authors present this as a route toward sub-milliHartree chemical accuracy.

entry.title: A rhombic spin-1 model explaining a room-temperature GaN emitter's magnetic resonance lines
entry.summary: A rhombic spin-1 interpretation of a room-temperature GaN emitter arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies optically detected magnetic resonance from single defects in GaN at room temperature. It argues that a minimal S=3/2 model cannot explain a g≈4 line in a common defect class, and proposes a rhombic S=1 model that reproduces three line positions with rms errors of 8.1-9.8 MHz. The authors state that existing data cannot uniquely establish the S=1 assignment and propose a zero-field sweep to test it directly.

entry.title: The Fate of Quantum Magic: How a Non-Entanglement Quantum Resource Dies or Persists Under Thermal and Dynamical Evolution
entry.summary: Fate of Quantum Magic arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies quantum magic, a quantum resource distinct from entanglement that measures how far a state departs from states stabilized by products of Pauli operators. The authors develop a framework to evaluate magic in generic many-body states and examine how it changes under thermal and dynamical evolution. They report a thermal sudden death of magic in the transverse field Ising model, generic spin chains, and the Kitaev spin liquid, and discuss how magic equilibrates after quantum quenches. The paper also introduces non-local magic and proposes a way to witness volume-law frame-robust magic in quantum materials using neutron scattering.
