entry.title: High-bandwidth magnetic sensing with bulk diamond NV centers
entry.summary: High bandwidth heterodyne sensing with bulk NV diamond arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper presents a magnetic quantum sensor that uses heterodyne mixing under strong optical and microwave driving, reaching MHz-scale instantaneous bandwidth with 548 pT/√Hz sensitivity in bulk nitrogen-vacancy diamond. The authors then extend the bandwidth of a single resonance to 48 MHz using a strong magnetic gradient and many individually modulated microwave control fields. The peak sensitivity in this configuration is 8.5 nT/√Hz.

entry.title: Fully quantum diffusion model generating synthetic malware records, with limited utility and costly sampling
entry.summary: Fully Quantum Latent Diffusion for Synthetic Malware Records: Effective Denoising, Limited Class Information, and Costly Post-Selection arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces a fully quantum latent diffusion model that generates synthetic malware opcode-sequence records, using a parameterized circuit with one mid-circuit measurement and no classical neural layers. Across 17 malware families, the circuit cut denoising infidelity by 63%, yet classifiers trained on its records scored a macro-F1 of 0.11 on real records, below 0.44 for a classical diffusion model. The authors conclude that quantum generators of shareable security data need joint evaluation of utility, privacy, and sampling cost.

entry.title: Reducing Errors in Quantum Eigensolver Molecular Calculations Using Extended Random Phase Approximation
entry.summary: Mitigating Errors in Variational Quantum Eigensolver Calculations through Extended Random Phase Approximation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes an error-mitigation method based on the extended random phase approximation (ERPA) to reduce hardware noise in variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) molecular simulations. It reconstructs the two-particle reduced density matrix from approximate transition density matrices, with a DMRG calculation supplying a noise-free one-particle density matrix. Benchmarks on IBM quantum hardware for water double-bond stretching and cyclobutadiene automerization show energy errors reduced by orders of magnitude, and adding multireference adiabatic connection corrections recovers dynamical correlation.

entry.title: Execution bias and repeatability in molecular VQE energy evaluation on quantum hardware
entry.summary: Execution bias, repeatability and mitigation cost in parameter-frozen molecular VQE energy evaluation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper tests molecular energy estimates from variational quantum eigensolver states on two 156-qubit IBM Heron processors, Aachen and Pittsburgh, with parameters and circuits frozen. It compares raw measurements against zero-noise extrapolation and readout error mitigation in terms of residual error, cost, and repeatability. The authors find that a smaller statistical error bar does not guarantee a more accurate energy. They recommend workload checks and repeated measurements before taking additional samples.

entry.title: Tunable Floquet exchange spectroscopy using Hong–Ou–Mandel interference
entry.summary: Drive-tunable Floquet exchange spectroscopy with Hong--Ou--Mandel interference arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This theoretical study shows that delay-resolved Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) coincidence measurements can probe how Floquet driving changes two-photon exchange in a collectively coupled cavity. A frequency-entangled signal photon scatters from the driven cavity while its idler serves as a delayed reference, and averaging over an unsynchronized drive phase preserves exchange interference within each output order. Fourier transforming the coincidence trace reveals two drive-dependent exchange branches tied to the Floquet-polariton spectrum.

entry.title: The geometry of Floquet states: a study of the moduli space of periodic Hamiltonians
entry.summary: The geometry of Floquet states arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies the moduli space of periodic Hamiltonians with nondegenerate Floquet spectrum, called "good" Hamiltonians. The corresponding Floquet states give a geometric model of this space, expressed using configuration spaces, flag manifolds, and principal bundles. A corollary of the main result is the complete determination of the rational cohomology ring of the space of good periodic Hamiltonians. The paper also considers adiabatic driving of a one-parameter family of such Hamiltonians and proposes two conjectures describing the resulting asymptotic quantum evolution, as Floquet analogues of the adiabatic theorem.

entry.title: Using neural networks to infer how many times a quantum channel has been used
entry.summary: Inferring the Number of Quantum State Transfers with Neural Networks arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies repeated-use quantum state transfer, where memory builds up in the channel between uses because it is not reset. The authors train a simple feed-forward neural network that takes only the Bloch vectors sent and received in a single use of an XX spin-chain channel and identifies the use number with over 90% accuracy. Using the channel's U(1) symmetry to form a reduced two-component representation raises accuracy to about 95%.

entry.title: Gravity-mediated entanglement in interferometers with repeated splitting
entry.summary: Gravitationally Mediated Entanglement in Interferometers with Repeated Splitting arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes and analyses protocols with repeated splitting stages, each doubling the occupied paths, to generate entanglement between spatially separated masses mediated by gravity. The authors derive an exact lower bound on the change in negativity and an explicit condition for when an additional splitting stage improves readout. Numerical simulations show an advantage in positional negativity over the parameter ranges considered.

entry.title: Gravity Between Nuclear Clocks: Using Quantum Nuclear Energy Superpositions to Probe Short-Range Gravity
entry.summary: Gravitational Interactions in Nuclear Clocks arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies whether the mutual gravitational interaction among a large ensemble of nuclear clock nuclei could be observed. The authors analyze the gravitational redshift caused by neighboring nuclei and treat nuclear energy superpositions as gravitational sources, producing a quantum gravitational interaction between pairs of nuclei. They find that for a macroscopic number of nuclei, such as in a solid-state thorium clock, the resulting frequency shift may become non-negligible.

entry.title: Memory Effects Limiting Repeated Entanglement Distribution
entry.summary: Memory-Induced Limits on Entanglement Distribution arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies the practical limits of distributing entanglement through quantum channels reused without reinitialization. It shows that excitations left in the channel by earlier uses act as a memory source that progressively suppresses coherent quantum transmission. The authors derive an analytical lower bound on quantum capacity and combine it with a Holevo-Werner semidefinite-programming upper bound to define a capacity window.

entry.title: Key Performance Evaluation of Relativistic Quantum Key Distribution Through Turbulent Free-Space Optical Channels
entry.summary: Key Evaluation of a Relativistic Quantum Key Distribution Over a Turbulent Free-space Optical Channel arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper examines how atmospheric turbulence affects relativistic quantum key distribution (RQKD) over free-space optical links, for both single-photon and coherent-state versions. The authors build a model that adds turbulence-induced phase fluctuations to the key-rate analysis and run numerical simulations under realistic channel conditions. Turbulence lowers interference visibility and degrades performance, with the severity depending on the ratio of interferometer separation or time separation to Fried's parameter.

entry.title: Engineering Baths to Generate Multipartite Entanglement
entry.summary: Generating Multipartite Entanglement via Structured-Bath Engineering arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes a dissipative method for preparing genuinely multipartite-entangled steady states using independent local reservoirs, an Abelian strong symmetry, and temporal bath correlations. In interacting Ising chains, flat baths are shown to erase Ising-axis correlations exponentially, while structured baths convert temporal correlations into classical spatial ones that strong symmetry lifts into quantum entanglement. Engineering the bath spectrum lengthens the correlation length, enabling GHZ-like states to be prepared from separable initial states.

entry.title: A benchmark family of Ising models that can be solved exactly.
entry.summary: Generalized Mean-Field Ising Model as a Benchmark Family with Exact Solutions arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper introduces the Generalized Mean-Field Ising (GMFI) family, a class of densely connected, inhomogeneous Ising Hamiltonians whose ground states can be obtained exactly. The exact solution reveals hidden low-dimensional structure and allows a number-theoretic classification of system sizes and degenerate ground states. The family is used to benchmark quantum and classical optimization methods, including quantum annealing, D-Wave experiments, QAOA, and several classical algorithms. The authors report unexpected system-size-dependent oscillations in the quantum-annealing gap.

entry.title: Eigenvector-Continued Green's Function Method: A Fast Reduced-Order Approximation of Many-Body Green's Functions
entry.summary: An Eigenvector-Continued Green's Function Method arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper notes that emulating the Green's function with reduced-order equations is difficult because it contains a large amount of information, including one-particle spectra, the one-body density matrix, and the ground-state energy. The authors introduce a systematically improvable emulator based on eigenvector continuation and moment-matching. The resulting approximation is obtained by solving linear equations, which separates the computation into offline and online stages.

entry.title: Mixed-state topological transition in a non-Abelian Kitaev spin liquid with emergent supersymmetry
entry.summary: Mixed-State Topological Transition and Emergent Fractionalized Supersymmetry in the Non-Abelian Kitaev Spin Liquid arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies a topological transition in a mixed quantum state of the non-Abelian Kitaev spin liquid, driven by bond dephasing noise. The noise maps onto interacting fractionalized Majorana systems, allowing sign-problem-free Monte Carlo simulations. At an interface between topological and trivial Kitaev states, a gapless Majorana mode appears, and at the dephasing-driven transition this mode gains emergent N=1 supersymmetry. Simulation results agree with the exact supersymmetric values.

entry.title: A Primer on Instanton Physics: A Short Course
entry.summary: A Primer on Instanton Physics - A Short Course arXiv · Oct 29, 2026These six lectures were given at the University of New Brunswick from 6 to 21 October 2026 for senior undergraduates and beginning graduate students. They introduce instantons in quantum mechanics and quantum field theory. The first four lectures cover particle mechanics as background, and the last two cover applications in semi-classical field theory.

entry.title: Computing quenched thermodynamics of disordered spin models with a quantum circuit that uses an ancilla and imaginary-time evolution
entry.summary: Quenched Thermodynamics from Ancilla-Assisted Imaginary-Time Evolution arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents a quantum algorithm for computing quenched disorder averages in the transverse-field Ising model, with coupling configurations grouped into gauge classes. Approximate Gibbs states are prepared through ancilla-assisted imaginary-time evolution, and the ancilla measurement record indicates which gauge class each energy estimate belongs to. On a 3×3 open lattice, a one-step circuit resolves all sixteen flux classes, and thermodynamic integration yields a quenched free-energy estimate.

entry.title: Measuring the edge heat-transport constant of a Kitaev spin liquid from spectra
entry.summary: Gravitational anomaly spectroscopy of a Kitaev spin liquid arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes measuring the chiral central charge c of a two-dimensional topological phase from the spectrum of edge response to weak modulations of edge couplings, rather than through thermal transport. Using the Virasoro algebra, the authors derive absorption weights that depend on c and the mean edge energy, and build a combination equal to c. Numerical results for the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid are reported, along with robustness tests under coupling errors, interacting edges, and a quantum-processor protocol.

entry.title: Quantum algorithm for molecular geometries and reaction pathways on a quantum processor
entry.summary: Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization for Variable Molecular Geometries arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces VGSQD, a variable-geometry extension of sample-based quantum diagonalization that reuses quantum samples from a reference geometry for displaced geometries, reducing quantum cost. Using circuits of up to 124 qubits on the IBM Heron r2 processor ibm-quebec, the authors determine the equilibrium geometry and energy of the beryllium dimer and water. They also compute the minimum energy path and energy barrier of a hydrogen exchange reaction, with results comparable to CCSD(T) and DMRG.

entry.title: Quantum observables of nonperturbative superradiant scattering, a theory of how many coherent spins scatter particles collectively.
entry.summary: Quantum Observables of Nonperturbative Superradiant Scattering arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies inelastic scattering from N coherent spins or any two-state system, showing the scattering scales as N², so the Born approximation fails at large N even when coupling is weak. The authors develop a nonperturbative theory of this superradiant scattering and its backreaction on the spins. The theory is said to apply to searches for millicharged particles and to neutron and charged-particle beams that could test quantum protocols for detecting cosmic relics.

entry.title: Goldbach representations in quantum optics and metrology: linking prime-number splittings to photon statistics and precision limits
entry.summary: Goldbach Representations in Quantum Optics and Metrology arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper links Goldbach representations to photon-number statistics in a quantum-optical setup. An even-number Fock state is sent into a stochastic beam splitter with uniformly distributed transmissivity, and the two outputs are projected onto prime subspaces. Each successful outcome corresponds to a Goldbach representation, and the averaged detection probability is proportional to their number. Using the Hardy–Littlewood asymptotic formula, the authors show that fixed transmissivity yields standard quantum limit scaling, while an equal superposition of representations yields Heisenberg scaling in phase estimation.

entry.title: Comparing homodyne and heterodyne detection for classifying optical quantum state families from finite detection records
entry.summary: Homodyne versus heterodyne detection for classifying families of optical quantum states from finite records of detection events arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper compares heterodyne detection with homodyne detection (using filtered back-projection to reconstruct the Wigner function) for identifying one of seven optical quantum state families, including GKP states, from finite detection records. With convolutional networks at N=100 events and 20% dephasing in the first family set, heterodyne detection outperformed homodyne by 14.1 percentage points, a difference that remains significant after multiple-comparison adjustment. At N=10^3 and 10^4 no significant difference was found, and the results concern a reconstruction-based pipeline rather than homodyne detection in general.

entry.title: Using cold atoms in optical tweezers to search for micron-scale fifth forces
entry.summary: Probing micron-range fifth forces with cold atoms in optical tweezer arrays arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper proposes a new method for searching for fifth forces at micron scales by resonantly exciting the motion of ground-state-cooled atoms held in optical tweezer arrays. The authors develop a homodyne readout protocol based on sideband thermometry that can approach the Standard Quantum Limit. According to the paper, this raises the discovery reach for fifth forces by up to four orders of magnitude over existing constraints, and can also probe extra-dimension models beyond the current tabletop state of the art through the parametric enhancement of higher-dimensional gravity.

entry.title: Quantum privacy amplification using hyperentanglement for quantum and classical signals sharing fiber networks
entry.summary: Hyperentanglement-enabled Quantum Privacy Amplification for Classical-Quantum Coexistence in Fiber Networks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses how Raman scattering noise from high-power classical traffic degrades quantum signals in shared fiber networks. It implements single-copy entanglement distillation using energy-time and frequency hyperentanglement to perform quantum privacy amplification at the physical layer. The method discards uncorrelated Raman photons by exploiting frequency anti-correlations of down-conversion. In a 20 km fiber testbed, the tolerance to classical launch power improved by 4 dB, extending the secure key threshold from -13.3 dBm to -9.3 dBm.

entry.title: Experimental methods for building quantum gates on superconducting NISQ hardware
entry.summary: Quantum Gate Engineering in Superconducting NISQ Platforms: Experimental Methods and Emerging Directions arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This review guides researchers and engineers through implementing quantum gates on superconducting NISQ devices. It compares conventional transmons with alternative superconducting qubit and processor designs. It describes how single- and two-qubit operations are built with microwave and flux pulses, including calibration workflows, and how truth tables and quantum process tomography are used for benchmarking.

entry.title: Competition and cancellation in a tilted Rice–Mele chain: exact Wannier–Stark offset
entry.summary: Competition and cancellation in a tilted Rice--Mele chain: exact Wannier--Stark offset and spectral readout arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies the staggered offset A in the Wannier–Stark ladder of a tilted Rice–Mele chain, which arises from competition between staggered onsite energy and dimerized hopping. The authors determine A using a strong-field series and a two-band Floquet expression, and show that cancellation restores equidistant spectral levels. They also describe how the offset can be read from the static spectrum on odd-length chains and how cancellation appears as two sidebands merging into one line.

entry.title: Pulse-Informed Placement of Parallel Two-Qubit Gates in Qubit Arrays
entry.summary: Pulse-Informed Physical Placement for Parallel Two-Qubit Gates in Qubit Arrays arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to choose physical couplers and design simultaneous control pulses for parallel controlled-Z gates in heterogeneous frequency-tunable transmon arrays. The authors combine a structural quantum multi-domain matrix (QMDM) with quantum optimal control, ranking and promoting candidate placements based on the pulses optimized for each one. On 30 held-out synthetic 3×3 processors, the median final projected fidelity was 0.993826 for pulse-informed placement versus 0.984981 for calibration-based placement, using 59.1% fewer optimizer iterations than an exhaustive reference. The validation covers two simultaneous gates.

entry.title: Learning Grover mixers for constrained optimization: a study of training a quantum circuit to prepare feasible-state superpositions for improved constrained optimization.
entry.summary: Learning Grover mixers for constrained optimization arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes a two-stage variational method that first trains a parameterized quantum circuit, using an entropy-based cost function, to prepare a uniform superposition over feasible states. This circuit is then embedded in GM-QAOA as the initial state and, with its inverse, forms a Grover mixer. Tested on the Maximum Weight Independent Set and Multidimensional Knapsack problems, it consistently improves over standard QAOA for MWIS but gives only marginal gains for MKP, with advantages shrinking as problem size grows. The authors attribute this to harder mixer training and note a trade-off between performance gains and the extra training resources required.

entry.title: Collaborating AI agents that run autonomous quantum spin experiments
entry.summary: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents an autonomous research laboratory in which large language model agents review each other's work and can stop or redirect investigations. The agents study ensembles of quantum spins in diamond, deriving the minimum number of calibration settings needed to predict responses to a family of microwave pulse sequences. An initial experiment matched the predictions, but repeated reference measurements revealed signal drift, so the agents revised the protocol without relaxing their acceptance criteria. The revised experiment met those criteria and supported the theoretical predictions.

entry.title: Quantum communication via a state discrimination method
entry.summary: Quantum communication: a discrimination approach arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes a state discrimination approach to unassisted quantum communication over a noisy quantum channel. Building on the operational duality between entanglement recovery and state discrimination, the authors construct entanglement-generation codes with explicit decoders based on Petz recovery maps. The error bounds hold for any number of channel uses and are expressed in terms of Petz-Rényi coherent information. For product sources, the error decays exponentially at rates below the coherent information.

entry.title: Quantum query cost of finding tournament winners
entry.summary: Quantum Query Complexity of Tournament Solutions arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies how many quantum queries are needed to compute tournament solutions, which pick winners from the results of all pairwise comparisons among N alternatives. Classically these problems need Θ(N²) queries. The authors show the top cycle can be computed with Θ̃(N) quantum queries and a Condorcet winner found with Θ̃(√N), while finding a strong king needs Θ(N^{3/2}) queries.

entry.title: Automated Verification of Hamiltonian Simulation Using Quantum Signal Processing
entry.summary: Automated Verification of Hamiltonian Simulation by Quantum Signal Processing arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents what the authors believe is the first fully automated verification framework for Hamiltonian simulation based on quantum signal processing (QSP). The framework exploits the algorithm's structure, proving that the all-zero ancilla block is proportional to the target Hamiltonian and inferring the subnormalization factor automatically. It then verifies the QSP layer by extracting the implemented polynomial and certifying its approximation error. The implementation handles block encodings of Pauli-sum Hamiltonians with up to 256 system qubits.

entry.title: SeQUeNCe.DQC: A Full-Stack Simulator for Distributed Quantum Computing
entry.summary: SeQUeNCe.DQC: Full-stack Simulation of Distributed Quantum Computing arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents SeQUeNCe.DQC, a new top-level module in the SeQUeNCe package that compiles quantum circuits into network-aware execution plans and runs them using existing quantum-network modules. The authors validate it by reproducing a two-node trapped-ion Grover experiment and comparing success probabilities with a reported 71% benchmark. They also study how compiler strategy, topology, and memory capacity affect execution time and success rate, finding that hybrid compilers mixing TeleGate and TeleData outperform pure gate-teleportation strategies.

entry.title: QSoftCore: A Conceptual Model for Quantum Software Engineering
entry.summary: QSoftCore: A Conceptual Foundation for Quantum Software Engineering arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents QSoftCore, a conceptual model that reorganizes established quantum computing concepts from a software engineering perspective. It links quantum applications, computational problems, algorithms, configurations, programs, and paradigm-specific computation specifications with state evolution, execution results, and backends. The authors report that the model provides shared referents for computations, executions, deployment configurations, backends, and measurement evidence across the quantum software engineering lifecycle.

entry.title: Quantum relay optical link using squeezed signals and energy harvesting
entry.summary: Time-Switching Energy-Harvesting Quantum Relay-Assisted FSO Communication with Displaced Squeezed Signaling arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies a quantum relay-assisted free-space optical link in which a decode-and-forward relay is powered by time-switching optical energy harvesting and forwards data using displaced squeezed signaling. Turbulence-induced loss is modeled as a pure-loss bosonic channel with a truncated Gamma-Gamma transmissivity distribution. The authors derive error and fidelity expressions for coherent and squeezed hops and analyze when squeezing improves throughput.

entry.title: Robust optimization of repulsive Casimir forces in a biased-semiconductor cavity
entry.summary: Passive-reflector bounds and robust bilateral nonequilibrium Casimir repulsion arXiv · Oct 2, 2026This paper studies how to achieve nonequilibrium Casimir–Lifshitz repulsion in a planar stack of conductors, vacuum, and biased GaAs, framing the design as a robust constrained optimization under fabrication and drive uncertainty. In the optically thick-slab limit, the authors prove that a symmetric optimizer exists. At 300 K with gap uncertainty of ±10 nm and drive uncertainty of ±0.005, the optimized design gives a worst-case outward pressure of 2.257 mPa, and a finite-slab scattering calculation agrees closely with the reduced model.

entry.title: A quantum battery charged selectively by frequency through an anharmonic mediator
entry.summary: Spectral and Impedance Matching for Multi-excitation Charging of an Interacting Quantum Battery via an Anharmonic Mediator arXiv · Sep 30, 2026The paper studies a finite-time charging scheme in which a driven two-level system transfers nonequilibrium resources to an interacting two-qubit battery via a weakly anharmonic three-level mediator. The mediator's lower transition enables nearly complete single-excitation transfer, while a two-excitation cascade charges the doubly excited battery state with a modest efficiency reduction. Detuning scans quantify spectral tolerance, and the full charge-discharge cycle's energy balance closes to numerical precision.

entry.title: Limits on preparing light states via phase-space majorization
entry.summary: Fundamental limits on photonic state preparation from phase-space majorization arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies probabilistic conversions between quantum states of light, deriving fundamental bounds for both exact and approximate transformations. The authors develop a theory of weak, fully relative majorization that compares the disorder of phase-space functions. Focusing on Wigner functions in multimode photonic systems, they establish no-go results and tradeoff relations for conversions involving squeezed, cat, Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill, and Fock states. The work derives novel bounds and recovers known tight ones. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a phase-space relative majorization theory yielding new no-go bounds and tradeoffs for photonic state preparation, recovering known tight bounds.

entry.title: Toffoli gates with no spare qubits, and T-gate counts for Boolean oracles
entry.summary: Ancilla-free randomized Toffoli gates and the T-count of Boolean oracles arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies the T-gate cost of Boolean oracles in fault-tolerant Clifford+T circuits. The authors compute sampled parities in place on the gate's own controls, which removes the need for extra qubits once the gate is large enough, using about 8 T gates per bit of precision per random circuit. The same holds for exclusive-ors of affine subspace indicators. The paper also shows that a random set of fixed density needs exponentially many T gates at constant error, whereas an affine subspace of the same density needs a constant number. ★★★★ Notable: The authors remove extra ancilla qubits from the Gosset et al. randomized Toffoli construction, using about 8 T gates per bit of precision, and compare against lower bounds.

entry.title: Coherent errors, syndrome extraction, and magic robustness in stabiliser codes
entry.summary: Coherent errors, syndrome extraction and the Robustness of Magic in stabiliser codes arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how coherent errors change the magic of states encoded in stabiliser codes, measured by the Robustness of Magic. The authors show that a unitary error adds one copy of the error's Choi state to the encoded magic, and that syndrome extraction removes this copy, restoring the logical robustness. They also give magic lifetimes for stored single-qubit magic states under Pauli noise, reporting that choosing the plane of the stored state extends these lifetimes about 1.5x on rotated surface codes under low code-capacity depolarising noise.

entry.title: Using memory effects to boost quantum-battery capacity
entry.summary: Harnessing Non-Markovian Memory for Quantum-Battery Capacity arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies whether the memory in non-Markovian dynamics can be actively used to increase quantum-battery capacity, taking a thermodynamic view. Within the process-tensor framework, it compares memoryless and memory-enhanced strategies and defines their gap as a memory-assisted capacity advantage. The authors prove this advantage vanishes for Markovian process tensors and is bounded by a trace-distance measure of non-Markovianity. A continuous-time example with random telegraph dephasing shows that memory built up during evolution can improve capacity retention.

entry.title: Tan's contact in trapped spin-orbit-coupled Fermi gases at finite temperature, a measure linking many-body and two-body quantum behavior.
entry.summary: Tan's Contact for Trapped Spin-Orbit-Coupled Fermi Gases at Finite Temperature arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper uses path integral Monte Carlo simulations to study Tan's contact in spin-orbit-coupled Fermi gases at finite temperature. Previous work covered only zero temperature. The authors find that thermal effects change how the contact scales with spin-orbit coupling strength, weakening the linear relation seen at zero temperature and producing a non-monotonic dependence.

entry.title: Coherent electron lensing in superconducting graphene junctions
entry.summary: Coherent Electronic Lensing in Proximitized Graphene arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper uses scanning gate microscopy (SGM) to study Fabry-Pérot interference in a ballistic graphene Josephson junction. Spatial maps reveal circular interference fringes caused by two effects of the tip potential: a global shift of the Fermi wave vector and a local perturbation that adds oscillations. An analytical model attributes the local response to coherent electron lensing, where the tip changes the phase along interfering paths. The authors show this affects superconducting transport and establish SGM as a tunable local lens for controlling interference in such devices.

entry.title: Input allocation for quantum systems based on controllability
entry.summary: Controllability-Based Input Allocation in Quantum System arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how local perturbations propagate through quantum dynamics governed by the Schrödinger equation. It introduces a volumetric controllability allocation score (V-CAS), computed from a multiobservable quantum-control Gramian via simplex-constrained log-determinant optimization over virtual local Hamiltonian perturbations. The authors give a matrix-product-state implementation with an error bound, and numerical experiments show the score identifies finite-time influence patterns different from correlation- and entanglement-based measures.

entry.title: Geometry of Magic Robustness and Directed State Conversion
entry.summary: Robustness of Magic and the Directed Geometry of State Conversion arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces a state-space distance calibrated by stabilizer states, based on the dual structure of the robustness of magic (RoM), and shows that RoM equals the distance to the set of free states. It extends this geometry to state conversion by defining a directed conversion deficiency, the distance from a target state to the states freely reachable from a given input. For single-qubit systems, the authors analytically construct a continuous family of mixed states with identical RoM but asymmetric convertibility.

entry.title: Revisiting the fermionic Unruh effect: entanglement and correlation under symmetric transformations
entry.summary: Fermionic Unruh effect revisited: Entanglement and correlation dynamics under symmetric transformations arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines how the vacuum seen by a uniformly accelerated observer affects quantum correlations shared with an inertial partner. The authors introduce a symmetric Unruh-like map that yields, for a Bell state, a bit-flip channel whose flip probability is the Fermi-Dirac occupation at the Unruh temperature. Using negativity, mutual information, and all six pairwise quantum discords, they find that entanglement and discord between the inertial observer and the accessible mode both vanish at infinite acceleration, leaving one bit of classical correlation.

entry.title: How Spectral Reduction Selects the Observable Imprint of Dirac Quantum Geometry
entry.summary: Spectral Reduction Selects the Observable Imprint of Dirac Quantum Geometry arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines how fixing the energy in relativistic electron vortices changes the observable signature of quantum geometry. The authors derive a Hermitian selection rule for first-order observables in momentum-dependent internal subspaces and show that the magnetic correction for the free positive-energy Dirac doublet is an exact non-Abelian Berry-curvature contraction. Changing the relative phase between the two spinor components switches this correction from zero in a conserved transverse-helicity sector to a finite value in a radial coherent superposition.

entry.title: Quantum change point metrology: extra Bayes risk of locating a change point and estimating its amplitude in one measurement
entry.summary: Quantum change point metrology arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper quantifies the extra Bayes risk of locating a quantum change point and estimating its amplitude with a single measurement when both parameters are unknown. It analyzes recovery conditions and cost scaling for ideal steps, finite offset prior width, and a quintic profile. It also examines a common optimum under quadratic position loss within the covariant class.

entry.title: Hierarchical Quantum Optimization That Solves Problems Larger Than the Qubit Limit
entry.summary: Symmetry-Preserving Hierarchical Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm with Subproblems Beyond the Qubit Limit arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes symmetry-preserving hierarchical QAOA (SP-HQAOA), which uses parity sector contraction to keep the zero-field Ising structure of the objective at each step, so each quantum call uses at most Q qubits even when leaf blocks exceed Q. The authors give a deterministic bound on the optimal-value loss from each sector restriction, and these bounds can be summed across contraction steps and hierarchy levels. At depth p=1, the method reaches 99.4% to 99.7% of the exact optimum on 40-node random regular MaxCut leaf blocks, and 96% of a classical reference for N=500 using at most 10 qubits per circuit.

entry.title: Einstein metrics and quantum control on a symmetric quotient of unitaries
entry.summary: Einstein Metrics and Quantum Control on Symmetric Tensor Product Quotients arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies the quotient space M_n of projective n-qubit unitaries by local unitaries and qubit permutations. For sufficiently large n, it proves that M_n admits exactly two PU(2^n)-invariant Einstein metrics up to scaling. After normalizing two-qubit costs, both metrics have uniformly bounded diameter, even though approximating a Haar-random unitary requires exponentially many two-qubit gates.

entry.title: Time evolution in multi-component dynamical Keldysh models, a study of how quantum systems evolve under long-correlated random noise.
entry.summary: Time evolution in the multi-component dynamical Keldysh models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper constructs a time evolution operator for dynamical quantum models driven by a multi-component random Gaussian field with a long correlation time. It analyzes three cases: a non-Abelian SU(2) symmetry class for three-component noise, and Abelian U(1) and Z2 classes for two- and one-component noise. The authors derive and solve coupled linear differential equations for exact diagonal and off-diagonal single-particle Green's functions, and use a continued fractions method to handle finite time correlations in Keldysh models.

entry.title: Exact, Scalable Quantum Optimization Gradients from Strict Causal Light-Cone Frequency Bandwidths
entry.summary: Strict Frequency Bandwidths from Causal Light Cones Enable Scalable Exact Gradient Evaluation in Quantum Optimization arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper shows that in layered quantum circuits built from commuting local terms, strict Heisenberg light cones limit energy slices to finite Fourier bandwidths when a shared layer parameter is varied. This allows exact gradient evaluation via a multipoint parameter-shift rule based on the discrete sine transform. For QAOA on bounded-degree graphs at fixed depth, the number of distinct circuit settings needed for the derivative drops from O(m) to O(1).

entry.title: Maximally-matched mixture decoding for correlated atom loss in quantum LDPC codes
entry.summary: Maximally-Matched Mixture Decoding for Correlated Atom Loss in Quantum LDPC Codes arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses correlated atom loss at two-qubit gates in neutral atom quantum computers, where losing one atom often means losing its gate partner. The authors propose a maximal-matching-mixture (MMM) decoder that builds a per-readout decoding hypergraph from the maximum matchings of the graph of possible lost-qubit pairings. This hypergraph can be used with an ordinary belief-propagation decoder. On the [[144,12,12]] Gross code, MMM reduces the logical error rate by up to about 25x compared with a loss-unaware decoder and about 2x compared with the uniform-mixture baseline from Baranes et al. (2026).

entry.title: Active method for fast quantum state preparation and reset in atomic arrays
entry.summary: Active Approach to Fast Quantum State Preparation and Reset in Atomic Arrays arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies rapid preparation and reset of quantum states in a waveguide-coupled emitter array operating at low excitation. By decomposing the effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian into biorthogonal modes, the authors link relaxation speed to overlap with subradiant modes, and propose local-drive protocols for reset and Dicke-state preparation. The reported reductions in time are up to about 25% for reset and 45% for preparation.

entry.title: Noise propagation and effective channels in encrypted quantum cloning, a study of how errors spread through a quantum copying protocol.
entry.summary: Noise Propagation and Effective Channels in Encrypted Quantum Cloning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how noise spreads in an encrypted quantum cloning protocol by describing the protocol through effective recovery channels. It shows that the effect of noise depends strongly on which qubit it acts on, for example turning isotropic depolarizing noise into an anisotropic recovery channel in one case. The authors conclude that effective recovery noise depends on the noise's physical location and the protocol's structure, not only on its strength.

entry.title: Quantum advantage via designed beneficial dissipation from lossless dynamics
entry.summary: Quantum advantage by designing beneficial dissipation from lossless dynamics arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies whether passive loss, designed from lossless quantum dynamics, can improve an unconditional target. It derives a trajectory-level criterion and builds a response operator from the lossless dynamics, whose spectrum shows whether weak passive loss helps and whose principal eigenvector gives the optimal environmental mode. Applied to vibronically assisted transfer, the predicted mode is near-optimal at finite loss, giving an 8.73% enhancement over the independently optimized lossless benchmark, versus 9.52% under full finite-loss optimization.

entry.title: Experimental observation of a phase transition in error resilience on a superconducting quantum chip
entry.summary: Experimental Observation of Error-Resilience Phase Transition on Superconducting Quantum Processor arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Random unitaries spread quantum information across nonlocal degrees of freedom, protecting it from local noise, but this protection fails once noise becomes strong enough. This paper reports the first experimental observation of this transition on IBM's ibm_pittsburgh Heron r3 device with up to 26 qubits. The transition is detected using fidelity, Rényi-2 entanglement entropy, and stabilizer Rényi-2 entropy, with zero-noise extrapolation and M3 error mitigation. The fitted critical angle is about 1.01, below the theoretical value of about 1.14.

entry.title: A coherent neutron-nucleus hybrid system linked by the strong force
entry.summary: A Coherent Neutron-Nucleus Hybrid System Mediated by the Strong Interaction arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper describes a neutron-nucleus hybrid system formed by coupling a coherent ensemble of polarized helium-3 nuclei with free neutrons. The nuclei are prepared in a spin superposition, and a magnetic field splits their energy levels, so the nuclear phase is coherently transferred to the neutron, producing an intensity beat at the nuclear Zeeman frequency. The incident neutron is prepared in a spin-energy superposition, and the nuclear and neutron phases heterodyne to give a signal at the sum or difference frequency depending on their relative helicity.

entry.title: Telecom-band quantum dots on metamorphic InGaAs: coherent control and pure single-photon emission
entry.summary: Coherent control and high purity single-photon emission from telecom quantum dots on metamorphic InGaAs arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies InAs quantum dots embedded in relaxed InGaAs matrices on metamorphic InGaAs layers, aiming for emission in the telecom O- and C-bands. By comparing quasi-resonant and phonon-assisted excitation schemes, the authors separate excitation effects from intrinsic emitter properties. They report linewidths as narrow as 21 μeV, the disappearance of slow decay channels, and single-photon purity with second-order autocorrelation values on the order of 10^-2. Rabi-like oscillations are observed in both telecom bands, suggesting potential for quantum technologies.

entry.title: Exact positive-P simulation of open quantum spin systems using a generalized density matrix representation
entry.summary: Exact Positive-P Simulation of Open Quantum Spin Systems with Generalized Density Matrix Formalism arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes a phase-space representation that maps spin-1/2 degrees of freedom onto parameters of a local generalized density matrix (GDM) instead of SU(2) coherent states. In all stable regimes, the stable solutions match exact results up to stochastic sampling noise. The GDM approach combines with the bosonic positive-P representation to enable scalable simulation of coupled spin-boson systems, which is demonstrated on the Jaynes-Cummings model and a Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard lattice.

entry.title: Quantum key sharing over fading links with minimal eavesdropper leakage
entry.summary: Continuous variable quantum key distribution through a fading channel with minimal information leakage arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper analyses a continuous variable quantum key distribution protocol over a fading channel, a model for free-space links. The protocol was previously shown to eliminate eavesdropper information in pure-loss channels and minimise it in noisy ones. The authors find that it keeps strong performance under fading and outperforms comparable protocols.

entry.title: Sample Complexity of Generative Learning for Quantum Measurement Data
entry.summary: Sample Complexity for Generative Learning of Quantum Measurement Data arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents a bias-variance framework for choosing model capacity when learning a quantum measurement distribution from finite data. It decomposes the expected population KL error into a representation bias term and a variance term, deriving four scaling templates for the optimal error. For transverse-field Ising Born distributions, the independently evaluated bias and estimation cost are used to predict the optimal context radius and optimal error, with power-law decay in N in gapped regimes and inverse-power decay in ln N at criticality.

entry.title: Lowering the cost of purifying ancilla states for Majorana quantum computation
entry.summary: Reducing the cost of ancilla purification for Majorana quantum computation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper notes that braiding Majorana zero modes alone does not yield a universal gate set, so ancillary states are needed for extra operations. It adds an extra comparison layer to the purification of the non-Gaussian ancilla in Bravyi's scheme, so that the preparation error decreases cubically rather than quadratically. The authors also present a preliminary purification sequence and report a distillability fidelity under ideal operations.

entry.title: Ontology without states: a dynamics-first realist argument from PBR
entry.summary: Ontology without states: PBR as an argument for dynamics-first realism arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines the common reading that the PBR theorem shows a pure quantum state represents a physical property of the system, arguing this reading presupposes a state-first theory. It distinguishes state-first from dynamics-first physical theories and uses a recent interpretation of quantum theory as an example. The author shows a dynamics-first theory can explain the PBR correlations while keeping a broadly epistemic view of quantum states. The conclusion is that PBR poses a dilemma: either the quantum state is part of reality, or reality is not fundamentally made of states.

entry.title: Are quantum measurements universal?
entry.summary: Are quantum measurements universal? arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper revisits a 2014 result that the Born rule arises as a universal average over all ways of selecting measurement-interactions in an extended Bloch representation. In response to criticisms tied to Bertrand's paradox, it defines a universal measurement as one that is indifferent to any part of the interaction structure. It proves that every such indifferent universal measurement yields exactly the Born probabilities, with a unique average.

entry.title: Geometry of quantum teleportation in phase space: a study describing the standard teleportation protocol using deformation quantization.
entry.summary: The Geometry of Quantum Teleportation in Phase Space arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper formulates the standard quantum teleportation protocol within deformation quantization, using the Stratonovich–Weyl correspondence and star product on SU(2) coadjoint orbits. Each qubit is represented by a spherical phase space with the KKS symplectic structure. The authors construct phase space representations of the Bell resource, controlled-NOT and Hadamard operators, measurements, and conditional Pauli corrections, showing how the input qubit's Wigner function is redistributed through correlations and reconstructed at the receiver.

entry.title: Quantum Foundations Beyond Bell's Theorem: A Topical Review
entry.summary: Quantum Foundations Beyond Bell's Theorem: A Topical Review arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This review surveys recent no-go theorems that extend the methods and concepts of Bell's theorem to more complex operational settings, including independent sources, quantum networks, joint measurements, and multiple observers. The authors organize these results under a shared Bell-inspired methodology that goes beyond quantum nonlocality. They also show how richer operational structures change which physical assumptions can be tested.

entry.title: Exact verification of rotation circuits for estimating iron-sulfur cluster quantum phases
entry.summary: Exact verification of Givens rotation circuits for efficient quantum phase estimation of iron-sulfur clusters arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper addresses Givens rotation circuits, which account for much of the cost of published quantum phase estimation algorithms for iron-sulfur clusters. The authors propose an exact verification method that separates a fixed Clifford change of basis and tracks basis states and phases in the remaining circuit, using integer conditions to confirm correctness. Replacing only the rotation term lowers Toffoli counts by 9.5-14.3% on benchmarks including FeMoco, with the walk operator unchanged.

entry.title: Estimating ground-state energy on cat qubits: FeMoco-54 in 23.5 hours with 7,164 qubits
entry.summary: Ground-state energy estimation compiled on cat qubits: 7 164 qubits for FeMoco-54 in 23.5 hours arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents a detailed resource estimate for the sum-of-squares block encoding algorithm of Low et al. applied to electronic structure Hamiltonians, compiled for superconducting cat qubits. It gives closed-form costs for key subroutines and global layouts for repetition-cat and LDPC-cat architectures, combined with adder compilation from a companion work. Under stated assumptions, the authors report that FeMoco-54 needs fewer than 7,500 cat qubits with an expected runtime under one day per phase estimation run on the LDPC-cat architecture.

entry.title: Running Shor's factoring algorithm on cat qubits: resource estimates for breaking RSA-2048
entry.summary: Shor's algorithm compiled on cat qubits: 22 593 qubits for RSA-2048 in 3.14 days arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper gives an end-to-end resource estimate of Shor's algorithm on superconducting cat qubits, covering the mathematical description through physical qubit allocation and scheduling on a chip layout. The authors compile the main subroutines onto two architectures, one based on repetition cat codes and one on LDPC cat codes, and design primitives such as a parity-CNOT gate for cat qubits. Under stated assumptions of error-correction cycle time, reaction time and phase-flip noise, factoring RSA-2048 requires about 23,000 cat qubits and 3.14 days.

entry.title: Stellar Representation of GKP States on the Double Discrete Cylinder
entry.summary: Stellar Representation of Gottesman Kitaev Preskill States on the Double Discrete Cylinder arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper develops covariant integral quantization on a double discrete cylinder phase space with the torus as configuration space, yielding a Wigner distribution and a stellar representation. The phase space suits translationally invariant states such as Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states, which are central to fault-tolerant quantum computing. It compares zeros of the stellar representations of ideal GKP logical states and their superpositions, and examines how zeros of the vacuum and finitely squeezed GKP states move with peak and envelope widths.

entry.title: Exact Solutions for a Dunkl-Klein-Gordon Oscillator in Non-Commutative Phase Space with a Magnetic Field
entry.summary: Exact Solution of the (2+1)-Dimensional Dunkl-Klein-Gordon Oscillator with a Uniform Magnetic Field in Non-Commutative Phase Space arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper solves a generalized Klein-Gordon oscillator, built with Dunkl derivatives, in non-commutative phase space, both with and without a uniform magnetic field. The authors use the Seiberg-Witten map to extend the commutative system and obtain exact eigenfunctions and energy spectra, which correspond to generalized Landau levels when a field is present. They also compute the non-relativistic limit and show that the solutions reduce to earlier commutative Dunkl models when the field or non-commutative parameters vanish.

entry.title: Complex Langevin kernels for real-time SU(N) lattice gauge theory simulations in 3+1 dimensions
entry.summary: Complex Langevin kernels for real-time SU(N) lattice gauge theory in 3+1 dimensions arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies complex Langevin dynamics for real-time SU(N) gauge theories in 3+1 dimensions and introduces new kernel modifications for lattice gauge theory. Using the anisotropic kernel as a baseline, stable simulations of pure SU(2) gauge theory at bare coupling g=0.5 reach a real-time extent of 2β on a rectangular regularized Schwinger-Keldysh contour. A local, field-dependent kernel based on traced plaquettes extends this to 3.5β. The authors also generalize the drift-magnitude correctness criterion to kernelled dynamics.

entry.title: Parity-resolved many-body dynamics of a topological qubit hit by phonon pulses
entry.summary: Parity-Resolved Many-Body Kinetics of a Topological Qubit under Nonequilibrium Phonon Pulses arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how phonon bursts from ionizing radiation affect a Majorana qubit made of two 2-micrometer proximitized nanowires, causing excitation, relaxation, and loss of logical coherence. The authors combine a lattice Lutchyn-Oreg model, microscopic electron-phonon coupling, and parity-resolved many-body dynamics. They find that even without quasiparticle escape, phonons can retain logical-state information, leaving permanent coherence loss.

entry.title: Error thresholds of a new symmetry-enriched toric quantum code
entry.summary: Topological Quantum Error-Correcting Thresholds of a Symmetry-Enriched Toric Code arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies the error thresholds of a new topological quantum error-correcting code under independent bit-flip and phase-flip noise. By mapping the problem to classical spin-glass models, the authors find that with equal X and Z error probabilities, the vertex-syndrome threshold improves by 30% over the toric code while the plaquette-syndrome threshold decreases. Both thresholds rise when Z errors are less likely than X errors, reaching 0.5 when Z errors are absent.

entry.title: Entanglement measures and LOCC conversion criteria via Schur-Weyl duality
entry.summary: Entanglement measures and LOCC conversion criteria from Schur-Weyl duality arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents a method to optimize functions of the entanglement spectrum of bipartite states over mixed-state decompositions to arbitrary accuracy. The approach uses a convergent semidefinite programming hierarchy based on a polynomial basis and Schur-Weyl duality. It also computes non-polynomial measures such as the entanglement of formation and characterizes the dimensionality of entanglement. The authors further provide a hierarchy of certificates for LOCC non-convertibility from pure to mixed states, along with a heuristic for LOCC convertibility.

entry.title: Magic in Grover's Algorithm and the Role of Oracle Synthesis: a study of how the quantum resource called non-stabilizerness grows during Grover's search algorithm.
entry.summary: Magic in Grover's Algorithm and the Role of Oracle Synthesis arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies the non-stabilizerness, or "magic," that builds up during Grover's quantum search algorithm, measured relative to stabilizer states that classical computers can simulate efficiently. The authors derive an analytic prediction for the stabilizer Rényi entropy after each Grover iteration and show it stays intensive as system size grows. They also examine the extra magic introduced when circuits are decomposed into elementary gates, and check the case of the 3-SAT problem.

entry.title: Long-range toric code models that keep finite-temperature topological order in 2D
entry.summary: Long-Range Toric Code: Finite-Temperature Topological Order in Two Dimensions arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces two-dimensional toric code models with added long-range loop interactions. These models keep the topologically ordered ground states of the ordinary toric code while confining anyons at zero temperature. For sufficiently long-range interactions, the authors argue this confinement persists at finite temperature, giving finite-temperature topological order that acts as a self-correcting quantum memory. For shorter-range interactions, topological order signatures survive only up to an exponentially large length scale, yielding a partially self-correcting quantum memory.

entry.title: Lattice definition of 2-group symmetries and extraction of their anomalies
entry.summary: Defining 2-group symmetries on lattices and extracting their anomalies arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Ordinary 0-form symmetries can combine with 1-form symmetries to form a 2-group. The paper gives a concrete lattice definition for a class of finite 2-group symmetries using local relations among symmetry operators, which identify the Postnikov class that characterizes the mixing. It develops a method to extract anomalies in one spatial dimension by restricting symmetry operations to an interval and comparing their composition near the endpoints. Explicit qubit symmetry actions for a 2-group with G=Π₂=Z₂ are constructed in one, two, and three spatial dimensions.

entry.title: Barren plateaus in quantum linear combinations: interference and Lie-algebra control
entry.summary: Barren Plateaus in Quantum Linear Combinations: Interference and Lie-Algebraic Control arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how interference from coherently summing quantum circuits, known as linear combinations of unitaries (LCU), affects the training signal. For a single-pass LCU, the authors show that even when each branch has zero matrix mean, the total gradient variance is at least the branch variance times the fourth power of its coefficient magnitude. They also derive exact loss and gradient formulas for interference between branches, with a four-qubit matchgate example where the interference term is nonzero.

entry.title: A perspective paper on AI and quantum open-source software
entry.summary: Perspective on AI and quantum open-source software arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines how verification is needed for reliable AI-assisted quantum software development. The authors analyze public repositories, records from 110 repositories across five quantum open-source hackathons, and a survey of more than 1,600 participants. They propose verification practices and contribution standards requiring reproducible evidence, and discuss how quantum open-source software can support independently verifiable AI-driven research.

entry.title: Twisted Fourier analysis of quantum weight enumerators for quantum codes
entry.summary: Twisted Fourier Analysis of Quantum Weight Enumerators arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper builds a unified Fourier framework for quantum weight enumerators of prime-power-dimensional qudits, introducing Weyl power spectrum and Weyl-conjugation autocorrelation as a symplectic Fourier pair that yields the quantum MacWilliams identity. The framework extends to twisted Fourier transforms, including the Rains shadow transform, and shows that all such twists reduce to Weyl translations of two basic transforms. Using refined identities in linear programming, the authors obtain tighter bounds for binary and qutrit quantum codes, including nonexistence results for certain parameters.

entry.title: A lower bound on the region of non-distillable magic states
entry.summary: Lower Bound for Region of Non-Distillable Magic States arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies magic states, a leading approach to fault-tolerant universal quantum computation. It extends the proof of Campbell and Browne on bound magic states. The authors determine a lower bound on the region of states outside the stabilizer octahedron that cannot be used to achieve universal computation.

entry.title: Adiabatic tracking and optimal schedules for preparing Gibbs states on classical and quantum computers
entry.summary: Adiabatic tracking and geometric schedules for classical and quantum Gibbs-state preparation arXiv · Oct 5, 2026This paper presents a discrete adiabatic framework for preparing Gibbs states in classical and quantum optimisation algorithms. It proves a tracking theorem for time-inhomogeneous reversible Markov chains and derives schedules adapted to the spectral gap and energy fluctuations. Applying the discrete quantum adiabatic theorem to temperature-dependent Szegedy quantum walks, the authors state that under suitable regularity conditions the quantum cost scales as O(δ_min^{-1/2}), versus the classical O(δ_min^{-1}).]

entry.title: Exact analytical solution for collectively pumped superradiance in Dicke states
entry.summary: Exact Analytical Treatment of Collectively Pumped Dicke Superradiance arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies a group of N two-level emitters that decay collectively and are pumped collectively, staying within the symmetric Dicke states. The authors sum up the infinitely many quantum trajectories created by competing pumping and decay to obtain an exact finite continued fraction for the Dicke-state populations. They also give perturbative transient solutions for strong and weak pumping, along with relaxation eigenvalues and emission observables for balanced pumping and decay.

entry.title: Optimal quantum discrimination at Liouvillian exceptional points
entry.summary: Optimal quantum discrimination at Liouvillian exceptional points arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines whether exceptional points (EPs) in non-Hermitian systems help detect weak perturbations. In finite-dimensional Lindblad systems with a unique stationary state and nonzero relaxation gap, the authors show EPs give no fundamental advantage in how observation time scales with perturbation strength. However, by selecting perturbations that boost the quantum Fisher information rate, EPs can reach a set detection accuracy faster than a non-EP reference with the same decay rate. An optomechanical model illustrates detecting a weak force at an EP in less time.

entry.title: Repulsive Landau Interactions Between Fermi Polarons at Strong Coupling
entry.summary: Mediated Interactions between Fermi Polarons in the Strongly Interacting Regime arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies mediated interactions between quasiparticles emerging from a Fermi sea, known as Fermi polarons, using zero-temperature quantum Monte Carlo methods. The main result is that the Landau interaction between polarons stays repulsive across all coupling strengths on the polaronic branch in the strongly interacting regime. entry.title: Dynamical quantum simulations used as testbeds for quantum information
entry.summary: Dynamical quantum simulations as laboratories for quantum information arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper shows that dynamical quantum simulations built to compute response functions prepare many-body states that carry information beyond their original observable. Using local-pulse protocols for Green functions in finite XX and XXX spin chains as a case study, the authors encode a classical bit via opposite source rotations and track how this record spreads across local subsystems and how readily different measurements access it. They find that fermionic covariance reconstructs the signed response in the XX chain, while simple spin measurements recover more local information in the XXX chain. The analysis is extended to Bell state recovery, quantum communication rates, and bipartite and multipartite entanglement.

entry.title: Meet-in-the-Middle Compilation of the [CNOT] Class with Fibonacci Anyons
entry.summary: Meet-in-the-Middle Compilation of the [CNOT] Class with Fibonacci Anyons arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to compile two-qubit gates for Fibonacci anyons, where errors arise from leakage out of the computational subspace into a fifth fusion state. The authors build a GPU pipeline that searches braid group subsets for low-leakage representatives of the [CNOT] class, narrowing the search space to reach braid length L=72. They prove that leakage lies in Z[φ], that nonzero leakage has an exponential lower bound in braid length, and derive limit distribution laws.

entry.title: Recovering classical gauge geometry from quantum master constraints
entry.summary: Recovering classical gauge geometry from quantum master constraints arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper asks how the degenerate directions of classical first-class constraints can be recovered when quantum theory is taken as fundamental and the constraints are imposed through a single positive master operator. For a nonnegative master function whose zero set is a Morse–Bott critical manifold, the image of the linearized Hamiltonian vector field is shown to be the symplectic orthogonal of the zero set, with coisotropy equivalent to the linearization having square zero. Three realizations are discussed, including the spectral bottom for quadratic masters and results for the non-Abelian SL(2,R) model.

entry.title: Adaptive Information Mining: Reaching the Quantum Limit of Super-Resolution Imaging
entry.summary: Adaptive Information Mining: Approaching the Quantum Limit of Super-Resolution Imaging arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents Adaptive Information Mining (AIM), a framework that achieves super-resolution by refining measurements of incoming photons in sequence. A reconfigurable imaging system reshapes its measurement responses to maximize Fisher information. When imaging point sources, the authors report estimation errors 2 to 5 times closer to the fundamental quantum limit than traditional direct imaging.
